guides.title: AI, LLM & MLOps for Platform Engineers — InterviewHub

questions.q: How does a large language model generate text, and what are tokens and context windows?
questions.text: Transformers predict the next token from a probability distribution, one token at a time. The context window bounds prompt plus output; cost, latency and memory all scale with token counts. python -c "import tiktoken; print(len(tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base').encode('hello world')))" curl $API/v1/chat/completions -d '{"max_tokens":256,...}' Interview tip: Say you track cost and latency in tokens, not requests.

questions.q: What do temperature, top-p and top-k control, and how do you choose them for production?
questions.text: Temperature rescales probabilities, top-k and top-p restrict the candidate set. Use low temperature for extraction, classification and tool calls; higher for creative work. Change one knob at a time. curl $API/v1/chat/completions -d '{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":1.0,...}' vllm serve model --generation-config vllm Interview tip: Note that temperature zero is not a guarantee of identical output.

questions.q: What is the difference between pre-training, fine-tuning, instruction tuning and RLHF?
questions.text: Pre-training learns language and knowledge, instruction tuning teaches following requests, and preference alignment shapes behaviour. Most teams use prompting, retrieval and light fine-tuning instead of pre-training. huggingface-cli download meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct accelerate launch train.py --method sft Interview tip: Say that most production value comes from prompting and retrieval first.

questions.q: What is fine-tuning with LoRA and why is it popular?
questions.text: LoRA freezes base weights and trains small low-rank adapters, cutting memory and cost and producing tiny, swappable files. QLoRA adds 4-bit quantisation. Great for per-task or per-tenant adapters. peft_config = LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=['q_proj','v_proj']) vllm serve base-model --enable-lora --lora-modules sql=/adapters/sql Interview tip: Mention serving many adapters over one base model.

questions.q: What is quantisation and what are its trade-offs for inference?
questions.text: Lower-precision weights shrink memory and speed up bandwidth-bound decoding at some accuracy cost, mild at 8-bit and larger at 4-bit. Always compare against a baseline on your own evaluation set. vllm serve TheBloke/model-AWQ --quantization awq python -m lm_eval --model hf --model_args pretrained=model --tasks hellaswag Interview tip: Say you validate on your task, not on public benchmarks alone.

questions.q: What is the KV cache and why does it dominate GPU memory at long contexts?
questions.text: The KV cache stores keys and values of past tokens so decoding is fast, but it grows with sequence length and batch size and often outweighs the weights. PagedAttention, GQA, quantisation and prefix caching help. vllm serve model --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 16384 vllm serve model --enable-prefix-caching Interview tip: Say capacity planning for LLMs is really KV cache planning.

questions.q: Explain the difference between the prefill and decode phases of inference.
questions.text: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel and is compute bound, defining time to first token. Decode generates token by token and is bandwidth bound, defining inter-token latency. Optimise and size them separately. curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null -s $API/v1/chat/completions -d @req.json vllm serve model --enable-chunked-prefill Interview tip: Ask whether the complaint is time to first token or streaming speed.

questions.q: What are embeddings and how are they used?
questions.text: Embeddings are vectors where semantically similar items are close. They enable semantic search and RAG. Index and query must use the same model, and changing it means re-embedding everything. curl $API/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"text-embedding-model","input":"how do I reset my password"}' SELECT id FROM docs ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT 5; Interview tip: Mention the re-embedding cost of changing models.

questions.q: What causes hallucinations in language models and how do you reduce them?
questions.text: Models generate plausible text, not verified facts. Ground with RAG and citations, allow I-don't-know, lower temperature, validate outputs in code, add review for high-risk uses, and measure with an evaluation set. ragas evaluate --metrics faithfulness answer_relevancy grep -c 'I don.t know' answers.jsonl Interview tip: Say you measure hallucination rate rather than assume it is solved.

questions.q: Compare using a hosted API model with self-hosting an open-weight model.
questions.text: APIs offer top quality and zero ops but cost scales linearly and data leaves your boundary. Self-hosting gives control and lower marginal cost at steady volume but needs GPU operations. Abstract behind a gateway. litellm --model gpt-4o --port 4000 vllm serve open-model --port 8000 Interview tip: Recommend a gateway so the choice stays reversible.

questions.q: What is a mixture-of-experts model and what does it mean for serving?
questions.text: MoE models route each token to a few experts so compute per token is low, but all experts must sit in memory. Serving needs several GPUs, expert parallelism and good interconnects. vllm serve mixtral-model --tensor-parallel-size 4 nvidia-smi topo -m Interview tip: State clearly: compute is sparse, memory is not.

questions.q: What are context length limits and how do you handle documents that do not fit?
questions.text: Use retrieval for fact lookup, map-reduce or iterative summarisation for whole-document tasks, compress conversation history, and test accuracy because long contexts cost more and can miss details in the middle. python chunk.py --size 800 --overlap 100 doc.pdf vllm serve model --max-model-len 32768 Interview tip: Match the technique to whether you need facts or the whole document.

questions.q: How do you version and manage prompts, models and configuration as production assets?
questions.text: Prompts, model versions and parameters live in Git, reviewed and tested against an evaluation set in CI, pinned, rolled out with flags or canaries, and logged with each request for traceability. git log --oneline -- prompts/support_v3.yaml promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.yaml kubectl set env deploy/api MODEL_ID=model-2026-06 Interview tip: Pin the model; moving aliases silently change behaviour.

questions.q: What is a small language model and when is it the right choice?
questions.text: Small models offer low cost, latency and on-prem or edge deployment, ideal for narrow tasks like classification and extraction. Use a router to escalate hard requests to a larger model. ollama run small-model vllm serve small-model --max-model-len 4096 Interview tip: Propose a cascade; it shows cost-awareness.

questions.q: What makes a good production prompt? Describe a structure you would use.
questions.text: Role and objective, delimited context, task with constraints and missing-info behaviour, strict output format, and few-shot examples. Put stable text first, test on an evaluation set and version it. cat prompts/classify.yaml promptfoo eval --prompts prompts/classify.yaml --tests tests.csv Interview tip: Emphasise testing on an evaluation set, not one-off success.

questions.q: Explain zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting and when to use each.
questions.text: Zero-shot is cheapest, few-shot fixes format and edge cases at a token cost, and chain-of-thought improves multi-step reasoning at higher latency. Start simple and add only when evaluation shows a need. messages=[{'role':'system','content':'Classify tickets...'},{'role':'user','content':'Example 1...'}] Interview tip: Say you add complexity only when evaluation failures justify it.

questions.q: How do you get reliable structured output such as JSON from a model?
questions.text: Give an explicit schema, use structured output or function calling or constrained decoding, validate in code with retry and fallback, keep temperature low. Valid syntax is not the same as correct values. response_format={'type':'json_schema','json_schema':schema} vllm serve model --guided-decoding-backend xgrammar Model.model_validate_json(raw) Interview tip: Say you validate in code regardless of how well the prompt works.

questions.q: What is prompt injection and how do you defend against it?
questions.text: Untrusted text can carry instructions. Defend in layers: separate instructions from data, least-privilege tools, human confirmation for sensitive actions, validate inputs and outputs, monitor, and red-team. Assume the model can be fooled. garak --model_name my-model --probes promptinject grep -E 'ignore (all|previous) instructions' app.log Interview tip: Say design so a manipulated model still cannot do serious harm.

questions.q: How do system prompts, user prompts and conversation history interact, and how do you manage long conversations?
questions.text: The system prompt sets persistent behaviour, messages carry requests and the app resends history each time. Control growth with a sliding window, summaries and separate fact memory, and keep the system prompt stable for caching. messages=[system]+summary+last_turns(6) curl $API/v1/chat/completions -d @conversation.json Interview tip: Remember: stateless model means history costs tokens every turn.

questions.q: What is prompt caching and how can you design prompts to benefit from it?
questions.text: Caching reuses the KV state of a repeated prompt prefix, cutting latency and often cost. Put static instructions, tools and reference text first and dynamic content last; avoid timestamps near the top; track hit rate. vllm serve model --enable-prefix-caching curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep prefix_cache Interview tip: Say static first, dynamic last, and watch the hit rate.

questions.q: How do you test and iterate on prompts systematically?
questions.text: Maintain an evaluation set from real inputs and failures, run it automatically on each change, compare to a baseline across quality, format, cost and latency, change one variable at a time, and canary online. promptfoo eval --output results.json python eval.py --prompt v4 --baseline v3 git tag prompt-v4 Interview tip: Say the evaluation set grows from production failures.

questions.q: What is function calling or tool use, and how does it work end to end?
questions.text: You describe tools with JSON schemas, the model returns a structured call, your code validates and executes it and returns the result, and the model continues. The application, not the model, enforces security. tools=[{'type':'function','function':{'name':'get_weather','parameters':{...}}}] tool_msg={'role':'tool','tool_call_id':id,'content':json.dumps(result)} Interview tip: State plainly that the model never executes anything.

questions.q: How do you control cost and latency when prompts grow large?
questions.text: Trim input and history, constrain output, use prompt and response caching, route tasks to right-sized models, stream, parallelise, batch offline work, and measure tokens per feature with budgets and alerts. curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep -E 'prompt_tokens|generation_tokens' redis-cli GET resp:$(sha256sum <<< "$PROMPT") Interview tip: Name token metering per feature as the starting point.

questions.q: What are guardrails and where do you place them in an LLM application?
questions.text: Layered checks on input, around the model call, on output and around actions: injection and PII filters, schema validation, grounding and safety checks, allow lists and human approval. Measure catches and false positives. nemoguardrails chat --config=./config python guard.py --check pii --input msg.txt Interview tip: Mention the false-positive cost to show balance.

questions.q: How do you design prompts for classification, extraction and summarisation tasks differently?
questions.text: Classification needs clear labels with an unknown option, extraction needs a schema with nulls and evidence, summarisation needs audience, length and a no-new-facts rule. Evaluate each on a labelled set. schema={'invoice_no':'string|null','total':'number|null','evidence':'string'} python eval_extraction.py --gold gold.jsonl Interview tip: Mention nulls for missing fields to prevent invention.

questions.q: Explain retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and its main components.
questions.text: Ingest, chunk, embed and index offline; at query time retrieve, rerank, build the prompt and generate with citations. RAG adds fresh private knowledge without retraining, but retrieval quality dominates. python ingest.py --src docs/ --chunk 800 --overlap 100 curl localhost:6333/collections/docs/points/search -d @query.json Interview tip: Say retrieval quality is the thing that decides RAG quality.

questions.q: How do you choose chunking strategy and chunk size for RAG?
questions.text: Start with a few hundred tokens and small overlap, split along document structure, keep metadata, consider parent-child retrieval, and tune with a retrieval evaluation set rather than intuition. splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=800, chunk_overlap=100) python eval_retrieval.py --chunk 400 600 800 --k 5 Interview tip: Say you tune chunking against measured recall.

questions.q: What is hybrid search and why combine keyword and vector retrieval?
questions.text: Vector search handles meaning, BM25 handles exact identifiers; hybrid merges both with rank fusion for better recall and precision. Confirm gains with a retrieval evaluation set. GET docs/_search {"retriever":{"rrf":{"retrievers":[{"standard":{...}},{"knn":{...}}]}}} curl localhost:6333/collections/docs/points/query -d @hybrid.json Interview tip: Mention error codes and product names as the case for keywords.

questions.q: What does a reranker do and when is it worth the added latency?
questions.text: A cross-encoder reranker scores query and chunk together, so retrieving many and reranking to a few raises precision and cuts prompt tokens, at some latency. Use it when context noise hurts answers. scores = reranker.predict([(query, c.text) for c in candidates]) curl $RERANK/v1/rerank -d '{"query":"...","documents":[...],"top_n":5}' Interview tip: Say retrieve wide, rerank narrow, then check the latency budget.

questions.q: How do you choose a vector database or index for RAG?
questions.text: Choose by scale, filtering and hybrid features, operations and security, index type and cost; benchmark recall versus latency on your data. pgvector is often enough to start, and the index must be rebuildable. CREATE INDEX ON docs USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops); SET hnsw.ef_search = 100; Interview tip: Say start with what you already run, and benchmark on your data.

questions.q: How do metadata filters and access control work in RAG, and why are they critical?
questions.text: Store ACLs and tenant metadata with every chunk and filter at retrieval time using the user's identity. Never rely on the prompt for access control, sync permission changes and audit sources used. filter={'must':[{'key':'acl','match':{'any':user.groups}}]} SELECT id FROM docs WHERE tenant_id = $1 ORDER BY embedding <=> $2 LIMIT 5; Interview tip: Enforce permissions in retrieval; a prompt is not an access control.

questions.q: How do you keep a RAG index fresh and handle updates and deletions?
questions.text: Ingestion with stable IDs and content hashes, delete-and-reinsert per document, propagated deletions, freshness metadata, and blue-green rebuilds for embedding or chunking changes. Monitor lag and failures. sha256sum docs/*.md > manifest.new && diff manifest.old manifest.new curl -X POST localhost:6333/collections/docs/points/delete -d '{"filter":{...doc_id...}}' Interview tip: Blue-green indexes make embedding upgrades safe.

questions.q: How do you evaluate a RAG system, separating retrieval quality from generation quality?
questions.text: Evaluate retrieval with recall at k and MRR against labelled passages, and generation with faithfulness, relevance, completeness and citation accuracy, plus refusal tests. The split tells you what to fix. ragas evaluate --dataset qa.jsonl --metrics context_recall faithfulness answer_relevancy python eval_retrieval.py --k 5 --gold gold.jsonl Interview tip: Separate retrieval from generation so you know which to fix.

questions.q: Your RAG chatbot gives wrong answers even though the right document is in the index. How do you debug?
questions.text: Trace the failure stage by stage: was the chunk retrieved, ranked, included in the prompt and used? Fix chunking, hybrid search, reranking, context length or instructions accordingly, and add the case to the evaluation set. python trace_query.py --q 'How do I rotate keys?' --show-chunks jq '.retrieved[] | {id,score}' trace.json Interview tip: Walk the pipeline stage by stage and add the case to the evaluation set.

questions.q: What is query rewriting and when does it help retrieval?
questions.text: A model rewrites or decomposes the query into standalone, expanded or multiple queries before retrieval, improving recall in chat and complex questions at the cost of latency and possible drift. Keep the original query too. rewritten = llm('Rewrite as a standalone search query: ' + history + question) results = retrieve(q) + retrieve(rewritten) Interview tip: Keep the original query alongside the rewritten ones.

questions.q: How do you handle PDFs, tables, images and other messy documents in ingestion?
questions.text: Use layout-aware parsing and OCR for scans, strip boilerplate, convert tables to structured text with headers, caption images, split code by block, keep page metadata, and read samples of the parsed output. pdftotext -layout doc.pdf - | head -50 unstructured-ingest local --input-path docs/ --output-dir parsed/ tesseract scan.png out Interview tip: Say you read samples of the parsed output; silent failures are common.

questions.q: What is the difference between RAG and fine-tuning, and when do you combine them?
questions.text: RAG gives fresh, private, citable knowledge; fine-tuning changes behaviour and format. Combine them: fine-tune for how, retrieve for what. Start with prompts, add RAG, and fine-tune only for proven behaviour gaps. python finetune.py --method lora --data sft.jsonl python rag_query.py --q 'policy for refunds' Interview tip: Summarise: fine-tune for how, retrieve for what.

questions.q: How do you add citations and grounding checks to RAG answers?
questions.text: Give chunks IDs, require claim-level citations or an I-don't-know, then verify in code that IDs exist, link them to sources, and optionally check support with an NLI model or a second call. Citations aid trust but are not proof. answer = llm(prompt_with_chunks) assert all(c in retrieved_ids for c in extract_citations(answer)) Interview tip: Check cited IDs exist; models can invent them.

questions.q: How do you reduce latency in a RAG pipeline?
questions.text: Measure each stage, parallelise independent steps, cache embeddings and answers, tune the index and candidate counts, shrink the context, stream output and use prompt caching, with budgets tracked at p95 and p99. curl -w '@curl-format.txt' -o /dev/null -s $RAG/query -d @q.json curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep time_to_first_token Interview tip: Say you track p95 and p99 per stage.

questions.q: What is GraphRAG and when would a knowledge graph help?
questions.text: GraphRAG extracts entities and relations into a graph to answer multi-hop and global questions that chunk retrieval misses. It is costly and complex, so try it when evaluation shows such failures, ideally reusing an existing graph like a CMDB. MATCH (s:Service)-[:DEPENDS_ON*1..3]->(d:Service {name:'auth'}) RETURN s python build_graph.py --src docs/ Interview tip: Reuse an existing graph such as a service catalogue if possible.

questions.q: How do you secure a RAG system against data leakage and poisoned documents?
questions.text: Prevent leakage with retrieval-time access control, masking, encryption and retention. Prevent poisoning by controlling writers, scanning on ingestion, tracking provenance, separating data from instructions, limiting actions and auditing which documents were used. detect-secrets scan docs/ python ingest.py --deny-sources untrusted --scan-injection grep doc_id audit.log | sort | uniq -c Interview tip: Name indirect prompt injection via ingested content.

questions.q: What is an AI agent and how does it differ from a simple LLM call or a workflow?
questions.text: A call returns text, a workflow follows developer-defined steps, and an agent lets the model choose actions in a loop. Agents are flexible but less predictable, so use the simplest design that works and add limits. while not done and steps < MAX_STEPS: action = llm(state); state = run(action) Interview tip: Say simplest design that works: call, then workflow, then agent.

questions.q: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and why does it matter for platform teams?
questions.text: MCP standardises how AI apps discover and call tools, resources and prompts exposed by servers, replacing custom integrations. Treat servers as production APIs: authentication, per-user authorisation, validation, rate limits and audit. npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node server.js claude mcp add my-server -- node server.js Interview tip: Say MCP servers need the same security as any API.

questions.q: How do you design tools for an agent so it uses them correctly?
questions.text: Few, well-scoped tools with clear names and descriptions, typed schemas, concise structured outputs, actionable errors, idempotency, dry-run and confirmation for destructive actions. Refine from transcripts. {"name":"restart_service","description":"Restart one service in staging only...","parameters":{...}} pytest tests/test_tools.py Interview tip: Read agent transcripts to find where tool descriptions mislead.

questions.q: How do you limit what an agent can do? Describe least privilege for agents.
questions.text: Give each agent its own scoped, short-lived identity, read-only defaults, allow-listed tools and resources, a policy gateway, human approval for high-impact actions, a sandbox for code, full audit logs and a kill switch. kubectl create role agent-readonly --verb=get,list --resource=pods kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:ai:agent Interview tip: Put safety in the environment, not in the prompt.

questions.q: What is the ReAct pattern and how do planning and reflection improve agents?
questions.text: ReAct alternates reasoning and tool actions grounded in observations; planning decomposes tasks; reflection checks results. Bound them with step, token and cost limits, loop detection and external validators. if history[-3:] == [last_call]*3: raise LoopDetected() pytest -q # external check after agent edit Interview tip: Say external tests beat asking the model to be careful.

questions.q: How do you handle memory and state in agents across steps and sessions?
questions.text: Keep working memory small, store plan and progress externally with checkpoints, use retrieval-based long-term memory with deliberate writes, timestamps and per-user scope, and treat remembered text as untrusted. redis-cli HSET agent:123 step 4 plan '...' SELECT fact FROM memory WHERE user_id=$1 ORDER BY embedding <=> $2 LIMIT 5; Interview tip: Mention privacy, deletion and treating memory as untrusted input.

questions.q: What are multi-agent systems, and when are they worth the complexity?
questions.text: Multiple role-specific agents can specialise, parallelise and cross-check, but cost more and are harder to debug and secure. Start with one agent and split only for independent parts, permission isolation or independent review. python orchestrator.py --agents planner,researcher,reviewer --budget 50000 jq '.messages[] | {from,to,tokens}' run.json Interview tip: Start single-agent and justify each extra agent.

questions.q: How do you test and evaluate agents, given that their behaviour varies between runs?
questions.text: Build a task suite with automatic success checks, run each task multiple times for success rate and variance, track cost and safety violations, use sandboxed tools, review transcripts of failures and gate changes on regression runs. python run_evals.py --tasks tasks/ --runs 5 --sandbox jq '[.[] | .success] | add/length' results.json Interview tip: Report success rate across runs, not one run.

questions.q: How would you build an on-call assistant agent for SRE, and what safeguards does it need?
questions.text: Start read-only: gather alerts, deploys, metrics, logs and runbooks, then summarise cause and evidence with links. Add low-risk actions behind approvals, least privilege, audit and injection defences; validate in shadow mode first. curl $PROM/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])' kubectl rollout history deploy/api Interview tip: Say shadow mode on historical incidents comes before live use.

questions.q: What is the difference between synchronous agents and long-running, asynchronous agent workflows, and how do you run them reliably?
questions.text: Run long agents as durable jobs with a task ID, persisted state after each step, a workflow engine or queue for retries and resumption, idempotent side effects, budgets, cancellation, approval checkpoints and tracing. temporal workflow start --type AgentTask --task-queue agents --input @task.json temporal workflow show -w task-123 Interview tip: Name durable execution and idempotency keys.

questions.q: How do you observe and debug agent behaviour in production?
questions.text: Trace each run with spans for model calls, tools and retrievals including tokens, latency, versions and cost, with redaction. Dashboards and alerts on success, steps, tool errors and spend; keep transcripts to replay failures. otel-cli span --name tool.call --attrs tool=restart,status=ok jq '.spans[] | {name,duration_ms,attrs}' trace.json Interview tip: Say it is ordinary observability plus token and quality signals.

questions.q: What is continuous batching and why is it central to LLM serving throughput?
questions.text: Continuous batching adds and removes sequences at every decoding step, so the GPU never waits for the longest request. It multiplies throughput and cuts queueing. Tune batch limits with realistic load tests. vllm serve model --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 python benchmark_serving.py --backend vllm --request-rate 10 Interview tip: Say you tune it with a load test that matches real lengths.

questions.q: What is PagedAttention and how does vLLM manage GPU memory?
questions.text: PagedAttention stores the KV cache in fixed-size on-demand blocks mapped by a block table, eliminating fragmentation and enabling prefix sharing. That fits more concurrent requests per GPU. Watch cache usage and preemptions. vllm serve model --block-size 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep gpu_cache_usage Interview tip: Compare it to virtual memory paging to make it memorable.

questions.q: How do you choose between vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Text Generation Inference and llama.cpp?
questions.text: vLLM is the flexible default, TensorRT-LLM maximises NVIDIA performance with a build step, TGI fits the Hugging Face ecosystem, llama.cpp suits CPU and edge. Benchmark on your own model and traffic. vllm serve model --port 8000 ./llama-server -m model.gguf -c 4096 --port 8080 trtllm-build --checkpoint_dir ckpt --output_dir engine Interview tip: End with: I would benchmark on my workload.

questions.q: How do you scale an LLM inference service on Kubernetes, and why is CPU-based autoscaling a poor fit?
questions.text: Scale on queue depth, running requests, KV cache use or time to first token via custom metrics or KEDA, not CPU. Cold starts are slow because of GPU nodes, image pulls and weight loading, so keep warm capacity and cache models. kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 | jq . kubectl apply -f keda-scaledobject.yaml kubectl top pod -l app=llm Interview tip: Mention the multi-minute cold start as the design constraint.

questions.q: How do you reduce model load time and cold start for large models?
questions.text: Pre-provision GPU nodes, keep images small and pre-pulled, cache weights on local NVMe or fast shared storage in safetensors format, use quantised weights, avoid scale to zero for latency-sensitive services, and gate readiness on warm-up. huggingface-cli download org/model --local-dir /models/model kubectl apply -f daemonset-image-prepull.yaml vllm serve /models/model --load-format safetensors Interview tip: Break cold start into node, image and weights.

questions.q: What metrics do you monitor for an LLM inference service?
questions.text: Track time to first token, inter-token latency, error rate and throughput; running and waiting requests, KV cache use, GPU health through DCGM; tokens and cost per tenant; and quality signals. Set SLOs and alert on queue growth. curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep -E 'num_requests_(running|waiting)|time_to_first_token' dcgmi dmon -e 1002,1004,203 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv Interview tip: Say you alert on queue growth, a leading indicator.

questions.q: How do you serve many tenants or models efficiently on shared GPUs?
questions.text: Use multi-LoRA for variants of one base model, pools or on-demand loading for different models, and GPU sharing through MPS or MIG. A gateway enforces per-tenant limits, priorities and metering; dedicate GPUs where policy demands. vllm serve base --enable-lora --max-loras 8 nvidia-smi mig -cgi 1g.10gb -C kubectl get resourcequota -n tenant-a Interview tip: Name MIG for hard isolation and multi-LoRA for efficiency.

questions.q: What is an LLM gateway and what does it provide?
questions.text: A gateway provides one API in front of many models with routing and fallback, virtual keys and policies, quotas and cost metering, caching, guardrails and tracing. It needs HA and careful prompt logging. litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000 curl localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-team-a' -d @req.json Interview tip: Say it makes model changes invisible to application teams.

questions.q: How do you roll out a new model version safely?
questions.text: Offline evaluation with thresholds, shadow traffic comparison, canary with quality, cost and latency monitoring and automatic rollback criteria, then gradual ramp while keeping the old version warm. Version model, prompt and config together. kubectl argo rollouts set image llm-api model=registry/model:v2 kubectl argo rollouts promote llm-api curl -s $PROM/api/v1/query?query=llm_eval_score Interview tip: Shadow traffic catches regressions without exposing users.

questions.q: What is speculative decoding and when does it help?
questions.text: A small draft model proposes tokens and the large model verifies them in one pass, giving the same output distribution with up to two to three times lower latency when acceptance is high. Best for low-batch, latency-sensitive loads. vllm serve big-model --speculative-config '{"model":"small-draft","num_speculative_tokens":5}' curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep spec_decode Interview tip: Say acceptance rate decides the benefit.

questions.q: How do you implement streaming responses and handle timeouts and retries for LLM APIs?
questions.text: Stream with SSE, disable proxy buffering and raise idle timeouts, set separate connect, first-token and total timeouts, cancel on disconnect, and retry only transient errors with backoff, jitter and budgets. curl -N $API/v1/chat/completions -d '{"stream":true,...}' proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; Interview tip: Say disconnect cancellation saves GPU time.

questions.q: How do you run LLM inference at the edge or on CPUs, and what are the limits?
questions.text: Run small quantised models with llama.cpp or ONNX Runtime on CPUs or edge devices. Throughput is bandwidth-limited and concurrency low, so use it for private, offline or low-volume narrow tasks and validate accuracy on the target hardware. ./llama-cli -m model-q4_k_m.gguf -p 'Summarise:' -n 128 -t 8 lscpu | grep -E 'avx|neon' Interview tip: Position it for privacy and offline, not for high concurrency.

questions.q: How do you design disaster recovery and high availability for an LLM service?
questions.text: Multi-AZ replicas with spare GPU capacity, replicated versioned model artifacts, HA for vector DB and gateway, fallback models or degraded modes, health checks that test generation, load shedding, and tested failover. Reserve DR GPU capacity. kubectl get pods -l app=llm -o wide aws s3 sync s3://models-primary s3://models-dr curl $LB/healthz/generate Interview tip: Mention that GPUs may not be available on demand in a disaster.

questions.q: How do you schedule GPU workloads on Kubernetes? Explain device plugins and resource requests.
questions.text: The device plugin advertises nvidia.com/gpu, pods request it in limits, and the NVIDIA container toolkit injects drivers. Taint and label GPU nodes, and use MIG or time slicing to share small workloads. kubectl describe node gpu-1 | grep nvidia.com/gpu resources:\n limits:\n nvidia.com/gpu: 1 kubectl taint nodes gpu-1 nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule Interview tip: Say GPUs are integer resources by default.

questions.q: What does the NVIDIA GPU Operator install and why use it?
questions.text: The Operator deploys drivers, container toolkit, device plugin, DCGM exporter, feature discovery and MIG manager declaratively, keeping versions consistent. Check driver and CUDA compatibility and cloud-provider driver options. helm install gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator -n gpu-operator --create-namespace kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator kubectl get node gpu-1 -o json | jq '.metadata.labels | with_entries(select(.key|test("nvidia")))' Interview tip: List the components to show you know what it manages.

questions.q: Explain MIG, time slicing and MPS for sharing a GPU. When would you use each?
questions.text: MIG gives hard-partitioned isolated instances with predictable performance, time slicing is simple but has no memory isolation, and MPS runs kernels concurrently for better utilisation. Pick by isolation and predictability needs. nvidia-smi mig -lgip kubectl label node gpu-1 nvidia.com/mig.config=all-1g.10gb kubectl get cm time-slicing-config -n gpu-operator -o yaml Interview tip: Match each method to its isolation guarantee.

questions.q: How do you monitor GPU health and utilisation, and what do the signals mean?
questions.text: Use DCGM exporter for utilisation, memory, SM and tensor activity, temperature, throttling, power and ECC and XID errors. Drain GPUs with repeated errors, and correlate with queue and latency metrics. nvidia-smi dmon -s pucvmet dmesg | grep -i xid curl -s localhost:9400/metrics | grep DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL Interview tip: Say GPU utilisation alone is a weak efficiency signal.

questions.q: What is tensor, pipeline and data parallelism, and how do they affect inference deployment?
questions.text: Data parallelism replicates the model to scale throughput, tensor parallelism splits layers across GPUs to fit big models and cut latency but needs NVLink, pipeline parallelism splits by layers across nodes. Check topology. vllm serve big-model --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 nvidia-smi topo -m Interview tip: Say tensor parallel stays inside a node on NVLink.

questions.q: How do you size GPU memory and capacity for serving a given model?
questions.text: Weights are parameters times bytes per parameter, add KV cache for concurrency and context, plus 10 to 20 percent overhead. Then benchmark tokens per second per GPU at the SLO and size for peak plus failure headroom. python -c "print(7e9*2/1e9,'GB at fp16')" python benchmark_serving.py --dataset prompts.json --request-rate 8 Interview tip: Show the arithmetic: parameters times bytes, plus cache, plus headroom.

questions.q: How do you handle GPU node failures and drain them safely in Kubernetes?
questions.text: Detect with DCGM and error alerts, cordon and drain respecting PDBs, let inference drain in-flight streams with pre-stop hooks, resume training from checkpoints, then diagnose, repair and validate before returning the node. kubectl cordon gpu-3 && kubectl drain gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data dcgmi diag -r 2 dmesg -T | grep -i xid Interview tip: Mention checkpoints for training and drain time for inference.

questions.q: What networking matters for multi-node GPU training and inference?
questions.text: Use NVLink within a node and InfiniBand or RoCE with RDMA and GPUDirect across nodes, NCCL tuned for topology, multiple interfaces in Kubernetes, and locality-aware placement. Watch for wrong interfaces, RoCE loss and stragglers. NCCL_DEBUG=INFO python train.py nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 1G -f 2 -g 8 ibstat Interview tip: Say the interconnect often limits scaling more than the GPUs.

questions.q: How would you build a shared GPU platform for several teams? Consider quotas, queues and fairness.
questions.text: Namespaces with GPU quotas, priority classes, a queueing layer such as Kueue or Volcano with gang scheduling and fair-share borrowing, node pools by GPU type, notebook culling and showback. Dashboards expose idle allocations. kubectl get clusterqueue kubectl create quota team-a-gpu --hard=requests.nvidia.com/gpu=8 -n team-a kubectl get workloads -A Interview tip: Name gang scheduling and fair-share borrowing.

questions.q: How do you improve low GPU utilisation in a training or inference workload?
questions.text: Profile first. Typical fixes: faster data pipelines and caching, larger batches or continuous batching, fewer host-device syncs, overlap communication with compute, mixed precision, and balanced ranks. Measure throughput, not utilisation alone. nsys profile -o prof python train.py py-spy dump --pid $(pgrep -f train.py) iostat -x 1 Interview tip: Say you measure tokens or samples per second.

questions.q: What are the options for getting GPU capacity, and how do you handle scarcity?
questions.text: Mix reserved capacity for production inference, spot with checkpointing for training, and on-demand for bursts; consider specialised providers or owned hardware at high steady use. Cut demand with quantisation, smaller models and routing. aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-DB2E81BA kubectl get nodes -l node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=p4d.24xlarge Interview tip: Say quotas and lead times are part of capacity planning.

questions.q: What is MLOps and how does it differ from DevOps?
questions.text: MLOps adds data, features, models and experiments to the versioned assets, data and model validation to testing, and drift and quality to monitoring, with retraining pipelines closing the loop. dvc add data/train.parquet && git add data/train.parquet.dvc mlflow models serve -m models:/churn/Production -p 5001 Interview tip: Say the new failure mode is silent quality decay.

questions.q: What does a production ML pipeline look like, from data to deployed model?
questions.text: Ingest and validate data, build features shared with serving, train with tracked parameters, evaluate against a baseline with gating thresholds, register, deploy gradually and monitor, with an orchestrator running it all as code. argo submit train-pipeline.yaml -n mlops kfp run submit -e prod -p pipeline.yaml mlflow runs list --experiment-id 3 Interview tip: Stress validation and evaluation gates; they are the ML-specific parts.

questions.q: What is training-serving skew and how do you prevent it?
questions.text: Skew arises when production features differ from training features. Share feature definitions through a feature store, use point-in-time joins, log served features and compare distributions, validate inputs and test both paths with identical examples. feast materialize-incremental $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S) python compare_dist.py --train train.parquet --serve served_features.parquet Interview tip: Say one definition of each feature, used in both paths.

questions.q: What is a feature store and when do you need one?
questions.text: A feature store provides a registry, offline storage for training, online storage for low-latency serving, point-in-time joins and freshness monitoring. Adopt it for reuse across models and real-time consistency; skip it for a single simple batch model. feast apply feast get-online-features --features user_stats:clicks_7d --entity user_id=123 feast materialize 2026-01-01T00:00:00 2026-10-01T00:00:00 Interview tip: Say it is justified by reuse and online-offline consistency.

questions.q: How do you use a model registry and track experiments?
questions.text: Track runs with code, data, parameters and metrics for reproducibility, and use a registry with versions, lineage, aliases and gated promotion. Deploy by alias so rollback is repointing, with access control and audit. mlflow.register_model('runs:/<run_id>/model','churn') mlflow models set-alias churn champion 7 mlflow artifacts download -u models:/churn@champion Interview tip: Emphasise lineage and alias-based rollback.

questions.q: How do you detect and respond to data drift and concept drift?
questions.text: Compare production feature distributions with a reference using PSI or statistical tests for data drift, and watch delayed accuracy and proxies for concept drift. Check upstream pipelines first, then retrain with gated validation. evidently report --reference ref.parquet --current cur.parquet --out drift.html python psi.py --feature age --ref ref.csv --cur cur.csv Interview tip: Say many drift alerts turn out to be upstream data bugs.

questions.q: How do you reproduce a model training run months later?
questions.text: Pin code by commit, version data with DVC or table snapshots, capture the environment by container digest and driver versions, log configuration and seeds, link everything in the tracker, and periodically re-run to verify. dvc checkout docker run --rm registry/train@sha256:abc123 python train.py --config cfg.yaml --seed 42 git rev-parse HEAD Interview tip: Say you actually re-run an old job to test reproducibility.

questions.q: Compare batch, real-time and streaming inference patterns.
questions.text: Batch is simple and cheap but stale, real-time serves per request with strict latency and higher cost, and streaming scores events continuously. Choose by freshness need and often combine batch with selective real-time. spark-submit batch_score.py --date 2026-10-20 kserve inference service apply -f model.yaml Interview tip: Ask how fresh predictions need to be before choosing.

questions.q: What is KServe and how does it help serve models on Kubernetes?
questions.text: KServe turns an InferenceService resource into a managed deployment with autoscaling, canary traffic splitting, pre and post processing and many runtimes including LLM servers, standardising model serving on Kubernetes. kubectl apply -f inference-service.yaml kubectl get inferenceservice -n models kubectl patch isvc churn -p '{"spec":{"predictor":{"canaryTrafficPercent":10}}}' Interview tip: Mention scale to zero and the cold-start trade-off.

questions.q: How do you orchestrate ML workflows with Kubeflow Pipelines, Argo or Airflow?
questions.text: Kubeflow Pipelines offers typed ML components with artefact tracking and caching, Argo is a general Kubernetes-native DAG engine, Airflow is a mature data scheduler. Choose by existing skills; keep steps idempotent and definitions in Git. argo submit --watch train.yaml -p dataset=2026-10 kfp run list airflow dags trigger train_model Interview tip: Say the choice follows existing skills, not fashion.

questions.q: How do you apply CI/CD to machine learning, including what gets tested?
questions.text: PR checks run unit tests, data validation and a training smoke test; candidate models are evaluated against baselines with gating thresholds; delivery uses staging, load tests and canary with rollback; retraining uses the same gates. pytest tests/ -q python train.py --smoke --rows 1000 python gate.py --candidate runs:/abc --baseline models:/churn@champion --min-auc 0.85 Interview tip: Name the evaluation gate; it replaces 'tests pass' for models.

questions.q: How do you manage data quality and validate data in ML pipelines?
questions.text: Validate schema, distributions, freshness and business rules at pipeline boundaries with tools like Great Expectations, block or quarantine on failures, agree data contracts with producers, and log results with model versions. great_expectations checkpoint run daily_orders soda scan -d warehouse -c config.yml checks.yml Interview tip: Say data tests deserve the same seriousness as code tests.

questions.q: What is LLMOps and how does it differ from classical MLOps?
questions.text: LLMOps versions prompts, indexes and tool definitions, evaluates open-ended output with curated sets and judges, meters tokens, adds guardrails and traces, and handles provider model updates through pinning and regression tests. promptfoo eval langfuse traces list --limit 20 git diff prompts/ Interview tip: Name the new assets: prompts, indexes, tools, guardrails.

questions.q: How do you handle model and data governance, lineage and auditability?
questions.text: Capture lineage automatically in the pipeline, enforce access control and audit logs, manage consent and retention, publish model cards, and align high-risk systems with frameworks such as NIST AI RMF and relevant regulation. mlflow models describe -m models:/churn/7 git log --format='%H %an %s' -- pipelines/ Interview tip: Say the platform should make governance records automatic.

questions.q: How do you control and cache costs of ML training jobs on Kubernetes?
questions.text: Use spot with checkpoints, right-size GPUs, queue and fair-share, efficient training practices, cached pipeline steps and datasets, and per-team cost tags and budgets. Reproducibility and caching are cost controls. kubectl get nodes -l karpenter.sh/capacity-type=spot python train.py --resume-from s3://ckpt/latest kubectl get workloads -n team-a Interview tip: Link reproducibility to cost: avoid repeating work.

questions.q: How do you build an evaluation set for an LLM application?
questions.text: Collect real inputs including edge and adversarial cases and past failures, define expected outputs or rubrics with expert agreement, slice by category, version it, keep it out of training and prompts, and grow it from production failures. jq -c 'select(.thumbs_down==true)' logs.jsonl > candidates.jsonl promptfoo eval -c eval.yaml --output results.json Interview tip: Say you feed production failures back into the set.

questions.q: What are LLM-as-a-judge evaluations and what are their pitfalls?
questions.text: A strong model grades outputs against a rubric, scaling review but with bias toward length and style, position effects and inconsistency. Use specific rubrics, randomised order, a different judge family, calibration against human labels and audits. python judge.py --rubric rubric.md --pairs pairs.jsonl --randomize-order python agreement.py --human labels.csv --judge scores.csv Interview tip: Say you calibrate the judge against human labels.

questions.q: Which metrics do you use to evaluate generation quality beyond accuracy?
questions.text: Combine task correctness, faithfulness, relevance, format validity, safety including over-refusal, style, operational cost and latency, and user-level signals. Avoid optimising a single number. python metrics.py --pred out.jsonl --gold gold.jsonl --metrics f1 schema_valid faithfulness jq '[.[] | .tokens] | add/length' results.json Interview tip: Present a scorecard, not a single metric.

questions.q: How do you run online evaluation, A/B tests and monitor quality in production for LLM apps?
questions.text: Log traces with versions, gather explicit and implicit feedback, score sampled traffic with judges and humans, A/B test variants with primary and guardrail metrics, and feed findings back into the evaluation set. langfuse scores create --trace-id abc --name helpfulness --value 4 python ab_analyze.py --exp prompt_v4_vs_v3 --metric thumbs_up_rate Interview tip: Mention guardrail metrics so an A/B win does not hide a cost or safety loss.

questions.q: How do you red team an LLM application?
questions.text: Define threat model and harms, attack with manual and automated techniques across injection, jailbreak, leakage and tool abuse, test the whole application, fix with layered mitigations, and add successes as regression tests; repeat regularly. garak --model_type rest --model_name app --probes promptinject,leakreplay python pyrit_run.py --target app --scenario data_exfil Interview tip: Say attacks become regression tests.

questions.q: How do you benchmark an inference service for latency and throughput?
questions.text: Model the production distribution of prompt and output lengths and arrival patterns, drive open-loop load in steps, record TTFT, inter-token latency percentiles, throughput and errors, and find the rate that still meets the SLO. python benchmark_serving.py --backend vllm --dataset-name sharegpt --request-rate 4 --num-prompts 500 genai-perf profile -m model --concurrency 16 Interview tip: Say the saturation point at the SLO is the number you report.

questions.q: How do you compare two models for a task fairly?
questions.text: Same evaluation set, controlled parameters, multiple samples with confidence intervals, blind grading, results sliced by category, and a full comparison of cost, latency, safety and licensing. Confirm in shadow or canary. python compare.py --a model-a --b model-b --set eval.jsonl --samples 5 --seed 1 scipy.stats.bootstrap((diff,), np.mean) Interview tip: Say your own evaluation beats public leaderboards for decisions.

questions.q: How do you test for bias and fairness in an AI system?
questions.text: Define affected groups and the fairness notion, test per-slice error rates and counterfactual variants, check generative outputs for stereotyping and refusal differences, mitigate, document in a model card, monitor, and involve legal and domain experts. python fairness.py --pred preds.csv --attr group --metric equal_opportunity python counterfactual.py --template tmpl.txt --names names.txt Interview tip: Say fairness is socio-technical, not only a metric.

questions.q: What is regression testing for prompts and models, and how do you automate it in CI?
questions.text: Maintain golden cases, past bugs and safety cases; on any prompt, tool, retrieval or model change run assertions and judge scoring against the main-branch baseline, failing on quality drops or cost spikes. Use a fast subset per commit and full runs nightly. promptfoo eval --ci --fail-on-error pytest tests/llm -q --maxfail=3 Interview tip: Say you compare against a stored baseline with a tolerance.

questions.q: How do you measure and reduce hallucinations in a customer-facing assistant?
questions.text: Define hallucination as unsupported claims, measure with answerable, unanswerable and trap questions plus faithfulness scoring and human sampling, and reduce it with better retrieval, citations, I-don't-know behaviour, tools, verification and human review for high stakes. ragas evaluate --metrics faithfulness --dataset qa.jsonl python verify_claims.py --answers out.jsonl --sources ctx.jsonl Interview tip: Say unanswerable test questions measure honesty.

questions.q: Walk through the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications. Which risks matter most for a platform team?
questions.text: Prompt injection, sensitive disclosure, supply chain, poisoning, improper output handling, excessive agency, prompt leakage, retrieval and embedding weaknesses, misinformation and unbounded consumption. Platform teams own agency limits, validation, retrieval access, supply chain and quotas. garak --model_type rest --probes promptinject,leakreplay,xss trivy image registry/llm-api:1.4 Interview tip: Say you check the current edition, since the list evolves.

questions.q: How do you protect sensitive data and PII when using LLMs?
questions.text: Classify data, minimise and mask PII before sending, pick deployment by sensitivity with residency and no-training terms, encrypt and tightly control prompt logs with short retention, enforce retrieval ACLs, filter outputs, and make the approved path easy. presidio-analyzer --text 'Call me at 555-0100' --language en aws bedrock put-model-invocation-logging-configuration --cli-input-json file://logging.json Interview tip: Say logs of prompts are often the largest leak risk.

questions.q: How do you secure the AI supply chain: models, datasets, dependencies and containers?
questions.text: Prefer safetensors, scan models, pull from trusted sources pinned by hash and mirrored internally, track dataset provenance, apply SBOMs, signing and admission policies to images, restrict egress and keep an inventory of model versions. modelscan -p model.pkl cosign verify registry/llm-server:1.4 --key cosign.pub sha256sum model.safetensors Interview tip: Say pickle files can execute code on load.

questions.q: How do you prevent an LLM agent or application from leaking secrets or system prompts?
questions.text: Keep secrets out of the model context, attach credentials in the tool layer, treat the system prompt as extractable, filter outputs and tool results, restrict egress, red team extraction attempts and use short-lived credentials. grep -R 'sk-' prompts/ && echo 'secret in prompt!' trufflehog filesystem prompts/ Interview tip: Say design as if the prompt will be seen.

questions.q: How do you handle prompt injection through tool outputs, web pages and documents the agent reads?
questions.text: Delimit untrusted content, separate privileged and untrusted contexts, require confirmation for sensitive actions, sanitise content, block exfiltration channels, run an injection classifier and log tool calls. Aim for containment. kubectl apply -f networkpolicy-agent-egress-allowlist.yaml python sanitize.py --strip-hidden-text page.html Interview tip: Say the goal is containment, not perfect detection.

questions.q: How do you secure model serving endpoints against abuse and denial of service?
questions.text: Authenticate through a gateway, rate limit and quota by tokens, cap input, output and concurrency, shed load, monitor for scraping and extraction, use TLS and private endpoints, and set budgets and autoscaling ceilings. limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=llm:10m rate=5r/s; curl -s $GW/admin/usage?key=team-a kubectl get hpa llm -o jsonpath='{.spec.maxReplicas}' Interview tip: Say token quotas and hard autoscaling ceilings.

questions.q: What is model poisoning and how do you defend against it in training and RAG?
questions.text: Poisoning corrupts training or retrieval data to change behaviour. Defend with trusted, provenance-tracked sources, anomaly checks, restricted contributors, clean evaluation and trigger tests, ingestion scanning, versioned data and quick removal. dvc diff HEAD~1 -- data/ python scan_ingest.py --src new_docs/ --check injection pii git revert <bad-data-commit> Interview tip: Mention versioned data for rollback.

questions.q: How do you apply authentication and authorisation for AI agents acting on behalf of users?
questions.text: Give agents their own identity and short-lived, user-scoped delegated credentials through token exchange, enforce authorisation in target systems and a policy layer, require step-up approval for sensitive actions, never expose credentials to the model, log both identities and support revocation. curl -X POST $STS/token -d grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange -d subject_token=$USER_TOKEN -d scope=tickets.read opa eval -d policy.rego -i input.json 'data.agent.allow' Interview tip: Say the agent must never have more authority than the user.

questions.q: What are the privacy and compliance considerations for AI systems, such as GDPR and the EU AI Act?
questions.text: Apply GDPR principles: purpose, minimisation, transparency, retention, security and data rights, preferring retrievable stores over weights. Prepare for the EU AI Act risk tiers with documentation, logging and human oversight, and involve legal early. python dsar_export.py --user 123 --stores postgres,vectordb jq '.records[] | select(.purpose==null)' processing_register.json Interview tip: Note that you are not giving legal advice and involve legal and privacy teams.

questions.q: How do you monitor and detect abuse or attacks against an LLM application in production?
questions.text: Log redacted traces with identities, detect injection patterns, extraction attempts, token spikes, unusual tool sequences and secret leakage, baseline per tenant, alert into SecOps with runbooks, and feed incidents back into guardrails and tests. jq 'select(.guardrail=="injection")' traces.jsonl | wc -l curl -s $PROM/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(llm_tokens_total[5m]))by(tenant) Interview tip: Say incidents update guardrails and the red-team set.

questions.q: How do you isolate and sandbox code execution by an AI agent?
questions.text:
Run generated code in a hardened sandbox, preferably a microVM or gVisor, with no credentials, restricted or no network, resource limits, a fresh disposable environment per session, dedicated nodes and network policies, and logged execution. kubectl apply -f runtimeclass-gvisor.yaml securityContext:
 runAsNonRoot: true
 readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
 allowPrivilegeEscalation: false kubectl apply -f networkpolicy-deny-all.yaml Interview tip: Say model-written code is untrusted by default.

questions.q: What is excessive agency and how do you design against it?
questions.text: Excessive agency means too many tools, permissions or autonomy. Minimise functionality, permissions and autonomy, add approvals, limits, logging and a kill switch, and test the worst case if the model is fully attacker-controlled. kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:ai:agent aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn $ARN --action-names s3:DeleteObject Interview tip: Frame the test as: what if an attacker controls the model?

questions.q: How do you secure the training and fine-tuning environment and the resulting model artefacts?
questions.text: Least-privilege dataset access with audit, isolated namespaces and egress controls, scanned images, workload identity, encrypted versioned signed artefacts in a controlled registry, hardened notebooks and monitoring of unusual exports. kubectl apply -f networkpolicy-training-egress.yaml aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket models --server-side-encryption-configuration file://sse.json cosign sign --key kms://... registry/model:1.0 Interview tip: Mention notebooks as the usual weak point.

questions.q: How do you build a responsible AI governance process that does not block delivery?
questions.text: Classify use cases by risk, provide templates, embed evaluation gates, lineage, model cards and guardrails in the platform, keep a small cross-functional review for high-risk cases with service levels, and measure and iterate. python risk_classify.py --use-case chatbot.yaml mlflow models describe -m models:/assistant/3 | grep -E 'card|eval' Interview tip: Say you make the safe path the easy path.

questions.q: How do you estimate and control the cost of an LLM feature?
questions.text: Model tokens per request times volume times price plus retrieval and infrastructure, validate with a pilot, then use right-sized models, routing, context trimming, caching, limits and batching. Meter per feature and tenant with budgets and track unit economics. curl -s $GW/metrics | grep -E 'tokens_(in|out)_total' python cost_model.py --in-tokens 1800 --out-tokens 300 --rps 20 Interview tip: Link cost to a business unit metric such as cost per resolved ticket.

questions.q: When does self-hosting an LLM become cheaper than using an API, and how do you calculate it?
questions.text: Compare API token cost with GPU hours, redundancy, storage, operations and idle capacity, using benchmarked tokens per second at the SLO and realistic utilisation. Self-hosting wins at high steady volume, with adequate small models or strict privacy needs. python break_even.py --gpu-hour 4.2 --tokens-per-sec 2500 --utilization 0.45 --api-price 0.6 python benchmark_serving.py --request-rate 8 Interview tip: Include idle capacity and engineering time in the calculation.

questions.q: How do semantic caching and response caching reduce cost, and what are the risks?
questions.text: Exact caching reuses identical prompts, semantic caching reuses answers for close paraphrases. Both cut cost and latency but risk wrong, stale or leaked answers, so scope per tenant, use TTLs, tune thresholds on evaluation data and exclude personalised requests. redis-cli SETEX resp:$HASH 3600 "$ANSWER" python tune_threshold.py --pairs paraphrases.jsonl --min-precision 0.98 Interview tip: Mention scoping caches by tenant and permissions.

questions.q: How do you route requests between models to balance quality and cost?
questions.text: Route by rules, difficulty classifiers or cascades that escalate when confidence or verification fails. Evaluate quality loss versus savings, log routes, add fallbacks and manage rules in a gateway. router.yaml: routes: [{match: {task: classify}, model: small}, {match: {task: reason}, model: large}] python eval_router.py --threshold 0.7 --set eval.jsonl Interview tip: Say you pick the threshold from measured quality loss.

questions.q: What are the main cost drivers in a RAG system beyond the generation model?
questions.text: Costs include embedding at ingestion and query, vector storage and memory-heavy indexes, reranking, parsing and enrichment, prompt tokens from retrieved chunks, and logging. Reduce with smaller or quantised vectors, caching, fewer better chunks and deduplication. SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size('docs_embedding_idx')); python dedupe.py --src docs/ --threshold 0.95 Interview tip: Say fewer, better chunks save generation tokens on every request.

questions.q: How do you implement FinOps for AI workloads, from tagging to showback?
questions.text: Enforce tags, allocate Kubernetes and GPU spend with OpenCost or similar, meter tokens at the gateway, publish unit-cost dashboards and showback, set budgets and quotas, then optimise idle capacity, spot use and reservations. kubectl cost namespace --window 7d --show-all-resources aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-10-01,End=2026-10-20 --granularity DAILY --metrics UnblendedCost --group-by Type=TAG,Key=team Interview tip: Say unit cost and value per dollar, not only total spend.

questions.q: How do you reduce idle GPU spend in a shared platform?
questions.text: Measure allocation versus utilisation, auto-shutdown idle notebooks, queue batch jobs with fair share, autoscale inference on queue metrics, share small workloads with MIG or multi-model serving, use spot, limit job duration and report per team. kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu")' dcgmi stats -e && dcgmi stats -v -j 1 Interview tip: Say visibility per team creates the incentive.

questions.q: How do you set up budgets, rate limits and kill switches to prevent a runaway LLM bill?
questions.text: Budgets and hard stops at the gateway, step, token and retry limits in the application, autoscaling and quota ceilings, cloud budget alerts with automated actions, scoped rotated keys and a tested runbook for revoking keys and degrading. aws budgets create-budget --account-id $ID --budget file://llm-budget.json --notifications-with-subscribers file://notify.json curl -X POST $GW/admin/keys/team-a/disable Interview tip: Say you test the kill switch with a simulated overrun.

questions.q: What is AIOps and where does it genuinely help SRE and platform teams?
questions.text: AIOps helps with alert correlation, anomaly detection, incident summarisation and context gathering, log clustering, triage and postmortem drafting. Start read-only, measure MTTA and MTTR, keep humans in control. amtool alert query --alertmanager.url=$AM promtool query instant $PROM 'anomaly_score > 3' Interview tip: Say you measure it against MTTA and MTTR on your own data.

questions.q: How would you use an LLM to summarise and triage incidents and alerts safely?
questions.text: Gather alert, change, related-alert, dashboard and runbook context, then produce a structured summary with linked evidence and uncertainty. Scope data, redact secrets, treat logs as untrusted, keep it advisory, and validate on historical incidents first. python gather_context.py --alert $ALERT_ID --include deploys,runbooks,owners python eval_incidents.py --history incidents-2026Q2.jsonl Interview tip: Shadow-mode evaluation on past incidents is the credibility step.

questions.q: How do you apply anomaly detection to metrics without drowning in false positives?
questions.text: Pick SLO-relevant metrics, use seasonal baselines or forecasting bands, require persistence and combined signals, tune sensitivity against labelled history, route low-confidence anomalies to tickets instead of pages, and learn from feedback. avg_over_time(http_requests_total[5m]) / avg_over_time(http_requests_total[5m] offset 1w) > 1.5 python seasonal_decompose.py --metric latency_p95 --period 168h Interview tip: Say not every anomaly deserves a page.

questions.q: How can LLMs help with log analysis, and what are the limits?
questions.text: Reduce first: template clustering, baselines and rare-pattern detection. Then use an LLM to explain errors, correlate by trace ID, summarise windows and draft queries. Limits: context size, misreadings, sensitive data and injection; keep humans responsible. drain3 --input app.log --output templates.json logcli query '{app="api"} |= "error"' --since=30m --limit=200 Interview tip: Say reduction comes before the model.

questions.q: How do you use AI to assist with root cause analysis across services?
questions.text: Provide dependency graphs, change timelines, golden-signal metrics, logs, traces and runbooks; the assistant ranks hypotheses with evidence and suggested confirming queries. Humans decide. Evaluate by replaying past incidents and measuring top-k accuracy. curl $TEMPO/api/search?tags=service.name=api%20http.status_code=500 git log --since='2 hours ago' --oneline -- deploy/ Interview tip: Say the assistant must show what it checked, not only a verdict.

questions.q: How do you use AI coding assistants safely within a platform engineering team?
questions.text: Approve tools and data policies, scan and review generated code, enforce plan review and policy checks for infrastructure, give least-privilege sandboxed access and no production credentials, and measure outcomes like cycle time and defects. semgrep --config auto src/ terraform plan -out=tfplan && conftest test tfplan.json gitleaks detect --source . Interview tip: Mention hallucinated packages and review of infrastructure changes.

questions.q: How would you build a natural-language interface to your observability data, such as text to PromQL or text to SQL?
questions.text: Give the model schema, metric descriptions and example queries, validate generated queries against allow lists, read-only access and limits, show the query with the result, ask clarifying questions, evaluate on execution accuracy and respect user permissions. promtool check metrics < metrics.txt curl $PROM/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="api"}[5m]))' Interview tip: Say you evaluate by execution accuracy, not string similarity.

questions.q: How do you automate runbooks with AI while keeping change safe?
questions.text: Make runbooks executable first, then let AI propose runbooks for human approval, automate only low-risk actions within allow lists, rate limits, blast-radius and freeze rules with verification and rollback, and expand autonomy as evidence grows. ansible-playbook runbooks/restart_pod.yml -e ns=staging -e pod=api-7f9 --check kubectl rollout status deploy/api --timeout=120s Interview tip: Say autonomy expands only as the track record justifies.

questions.q: What are the pitfalls of using AI for capacity planning and autoscaling decisions?
questions.text: Forecasts fit the past and fail on new regimes; feedback loops and opaque decisions complicate debugging. Keep min and max bounds, reactive fallback, forecast error tracking and human input for known events. Simple seasonal methods often suffice. kubectl get hpa -o wide python forecast_eval.py --pred forecast.csv --actual actual.csv --metric mape Interview tip: Say predictive scaling should only add capacity early, with a reactive backstop.

questions.q: How do you use AI to reduce alert noise and correlate alerts into incidents?
questions.text: Deduplicate, group by service and window, suppress child alerts, and alert on SLO symptoms. Add topology-aware correlation and model-proposed groupings that humans confirm. Measure alerts per incident and actionable pages, and never hide critical alerts. amtool silence query --alertmanager.url=$AM group_by: ['alertname','cluster','service'] Interview tip: Say suppressed alerts must stay auditable.

questions.q: How can LLMs help draft postmortems, and what must humans still own?
questions.text: Use a model to assemble the timeline, impact summary, action items and template checks from incident records, with citations. Humans validate facts, analyse contributing factors blamelessly, choose priorities and track the follow-up work. python build_timeline.py --incident INC-4821 --sources slack,pagerduty,deploys python check_template.py postmortem.md Interview tip: Say the model drafts, but people own the lessons.

questions.q: How would you build a Kubernetes troubleshooting assistant for developers, and keep it safe?
questions.text: A read-only assistant with vetted tools for describe, events, logs, usage and rollouts under the user's own permissions. It explains likely causes with evidence, treats logs as untrusted, audits use, and is tested on a library of known failure scenarios. kubectl describe pod $POD -n $NS kubectl logs $POD -n $NS --previous --tail=100 kubectl get events -n $NS --sort-by=.lastTimestamp Interview tip: Say read-only first, then confirmed actions with user permissions.

questions.q: Which techniques cut token spend without hurting quality, such as batch APIs, shorter prompts and context pruning?
questions.text: Measure first, then trim prompts, prune context, cap output, route to cheaper models, batch non-urgent work and cache repeats. Validate every change against the evaluation set and track cost per task. python token_report.py --group-by prompt_id --top 20 python eval_run.py --prompt v7 --compare v6 Interview tip: Say each saving must pass the evaluation set.

questions.q: How do quantisation and model size choices change the cost of serving, and how do you decide?
questions.text: Smaller or quantised models need fewer GPUs and leave more KV cache room, raising throughput. Compare full precision, quantised and smaller models on the evaluation set and benchmarks, and decide by cost per successful task. vllm serve model --quantization awq --max-model-len 8192 python benchmark_serving.py --model model --request-rate 8 Interview tip: Say you compare cost per successful task, not per token.

questions.q: How do you set up human review and labelling for evaluating an AI feature?
questions.text: Write a rubric with examples, pilot it, use qualified reviewers, measure agreement, sample randomly and by risk, blind comparisons, protect data, version labels and use them to calibrate automated judges and grow regression sets. python agreement.py --labels labels.csv --metric kappa python sample_for_review.py --random 50 --failures 50 Interview tip: Say low agreement usually means an unclear rubric.

questions.q: What is benchmark contamination and how do you avoid fooling yourself with evaluation results?
questions.text: Contamination inflates scores when test data was seen in training. Use private, recent test sets separate from development data, deduplicate against fine-tuning data, report confidence intervals and segment results, refresh sets and confirm with online tests. python dedupe_overlap.py --train ft.jsonl --test test.jsonl --threshold 0.9 python bootstrap_ci.py --scores run.csv Interview tip: Say report confidence intervals and per-segment results.

questions.q: How do you evaluate guardrails, including false positives and false negatives?
questions.text: Treat the guardrail as a classifier: a labelled set with harmful and benign look-alike cases, measure false negatives and positives per category and threshold, test adversarial variants, track latency, review samples in production and refresh the set. python eval_guardrail.py --set guard.jsonl --threshold 0.6 python roc_curve.py --scores guard_scores.csv Interview tip: Say you measure both blocked-good and missed-bad.

questions.q: How does the position of information in a long prompt affect results, and how do you structure long contexts?
questions.text: Put stable instructions first, delimit documents with identifiers, place the question after the material, order by relevance, ask for quotes before answers and trim context. Test answers at different positions and split tasks if quality degrades. python position_test.py --doc long.txt --answer-pos 0,25,50,75,100 python build_prompt.py --docs retrieved.json --max-chunks 6 Interview tip: Say you test answer position on your own model.

questions.q: How do you handle multilingual users in prompts and evaluation?
questions.text: Measure per-language quality, instruct replies in the user's language, use multilingual embeddings, build native-reviewed test sets, evaluate guardrails per language and track token cost, with stronger-model fallbacks where needed. python eval_by_language.py --set multi.jsonl --langs en,hi,te,ta python token_count.py --text sample_hi.txt --model m Interview tip: Say report per-language results, not one average.

questions.q: How do you choose and upgrade an embedding model without breaking a RAG system?
questions.text: Choose by recall and ranking on your own evaluation set plus dimensions, length, language, cost and licence. Upgrade as a migration: build a parallel index, shadow queries, switch gradually, store the model version with vectors and keep rollback. python eval_retrieval.py --model bge-m3 --set qa.jsonl --k 5 SELECT embedding_model, count(*) FROM chunks GROUP BY 1; Interview tip: Say vectors from different models are incompatible, so upgrades are migrations.

questions.q: How do you design multi-tenant RAG so tenants never see each other's data?
questions.text: Enforce isolation in retrieval: per-tenant indexes for strongest separation, or a shared index with a server-enforced tenant filter, or a hybrid. Add document-level permissions, scoped caches and logs, tests for cross-tenant queries and verifiable deletion. python leak_test.py --tenant A --query "tenant B salary data" --expect-empty curl -X DELETE $VDB/collections/tenant_b Interview tip: Say the tenant filter must be server-enforced.

questions.q: Where should human approval sit in an agent workflow, and how do you design it so people do not just click approve?
questions.text: Require approval for irreversible, costly, external or privileged actions, group steps into approved plans, show exact actions with previews and evidence, default to deny, log decisions, and track approval rates to detect rubber-stamping. agent run --require-approval 'delete,send_email,deploy' --plan-mode kubectl diff -f proposed.yaml Interview tip: Say show a diff or preview, not a vague yes or no.

questions.q: How do you make agent actions reliable with retries, idempotency and failure recovery?
questions.text: Use timeouts, bounded retries with backoff, idempotency keys for writes, checkpoints after each step, compensating actions for multi-step changes, bounded loops and a clear handoff on failure. Test with injected faults. curl -H 'Idempotency-Key: 7f3c-ticket-991' -X POST $API/tickets -d @t.json temporal workflow show --workflow-id agent-991 Interview tip: Say treat tool calls like any unreliable network call.

questions.q: How do you choose between building an agent with a framework and writing a thin custom loop?
questions.text: Frameworks speed up prototypes but add abstraction, churn and debugging cost. A thin owned loop is transparent and easy to control. Prototype quickly, keep the production core simple, use libraries selectively and keep tools, prompts and evaluations portable. while not done: resp = llm(messages, tools); run_tools(resp); messages.append(results) pip list | grep -E 'langgraph|langchain|llama-index' Interview tip: Say keep tools, prompts and evals framework-independent.

questions.q: How do you serve many fine-tuned variants efficiently with LoRA adapters?
questions.text: Keep one base model on the GPU and apply small LoRA adapters per request, loaded on demand from a versioned registry with caching. This serves many variants cheaply; merge very busy variants, evaluate each, and enforce adapter access control. vllm serve base-model --enable-lora --lora-modules tenantA=/adapters/a tenantB=/adapters/b curl $VLLM/v1/completions -d '{"model":"tenantA","prompt":"Hi"}' Interview tip: Say one base model, many small adapters.

questions.q: What is prefix caching, and how can KV cache offloading improve serving efficiency?
questions.text: Prefix caching reuses KV cache for shared prompt prefixes, cutting prefill time and cost, if prompts are stable at the start and routing is cache-aware. Offloading moves cold KV blocks to CPU or storage to hold more sessions, at some latency cost. vllm serve model --enable-prefix-caching curl -s $VLLM/metrics | grep prefix_cache Interview tip: Say keep shared text identical and at the start of prompts.

questions.q: How do you load test and capacity-plan an LLM service before launch?
questions.text: Use realistic prompt and output length distributions, ramp load in steps, record TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, errors and GPU and KV cache use, find the rate per replica that meets the SLO, add headroom, test overload and failures, and repeat after changes. python benchmark_serving.py --backend vllm --request-rate 4 --num-prompts 500 --dataset-path real.jsonl k6 run llm_ramp.js Interview tip: Say capacity is the highest rate that still meets the latency SLO.

questions.q: What is Ansible and how does its agentless architecture work?
questions.text: A control node pushes small modules over SSH or WinRM, runs them, returns JSON and cleans up. No agent is installed, which keeps onboarding easy and the attack surface small, at the cost of SSH latency at very large scale. ansible all -i inventory.ini -m ping ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml Interview tip: Say agentless plus idempotent modules, and name the scale trade-off.

questions.q: What is an inventory, and how do static and dynamic inventories differ?
questions.text: Static inventories are files listing hosts and groups; dynamic inventories use plugins to query AWS, Azure, VMware or a CMDB at run time. Combine both in a directory and check results with ansible-inventory. ansible-inventory -i inventory/ --graph ansible-inventory -i aws_ec2.yml --list | jq '."_meta".hostvars | keys' Interview tip: Say you verify with ansible-inventory before any run.
