questions.q: When do you use ad-hoc commands rather than playbooks?
questions.text: Ad-hoc commands suit quick investigation or incident actions with one module. Repeatable or shared work goes into a playbook, which is reviewable, versioned and supports variables, handlers and conditionals. ansible web -m service -a 'name=nginx state=restarted' -b ansible all -m setup -a 'filter=ansible_distribution*' Interview tip: Say if you run it twice, it becomes a playbook.

questions.q: What does idempotency mean in Ansible and how do you keep tasks idempotent?
questions.text: Idempotent tasks converge to the same state on every run, so a second run reports zero changes. Prefer state-based modules, use creates, changed_when and failed_when for command tasks, and test by running twice. ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff ansible-playbook site.yml | grep -E 'changed=[1-9]' && echo 'not idempotent' Interview tip: Mention the run-twice test in CI.

questions.q: How does Ansible compare with Puppet, Chef and Terraform, and where does each fit?
questions.text: Ansible is agentless, push-based and strong for orchestration and configuration. Puppet and Chef are agent-based pull tools with continuous enforcement. Terraform manages infrastructure lifecycle with state; use it to create, and Ansible to configure. terraform output -json instance_ips > ips.json ansible-playbook -i inventory/from_tf.py configure.yml Interview tip: Say Terraform creates, Ansible configures.

questions.q: How does Ansible choose configuration, and what is the precedence of ansible.cfg?
questions.text: The first config found wins: ANSIBLE_CONFIG, then ansible.cfg in the current directory, home, then system. Environment variables and flags override. Keep a project ansible.cfg in the repo and inspect with ansible-config dump. ansible-config dump --only-changed ansible --version Interview tip: Mention a repo-level ansible.cfg for reproducibility.

questions.q: What are facts, and when would you disable or customise fact gathering?
questions.text: Facts are host details gathered by the setup module at play start and used as variables. Disable them or limit with gather_subset to save time, cache them for large fleets, and add custom facts under facts.d. ansible web -m setup -a 'gather_subset=min' - hosts: all gather_facts: false Interview tip: Say gather_subset and caching are the scale levers.

questions.q: How do connection methods and privilege escalation (become) work?
questions.text: Connection plugins such as SSH or WinRM reach hosts; become escalates with sudo or su. Use a dedicated automation user with keys, apply become only where needed, and use a bastion through ProxyCommand for private networks. ansible_ssh_common_args='-o ProxyCommand="ssh -W %h:%p -q bastion"' - hosts: db become: true become_user: postgres Interview tip: Say least privilege: become only on tasks that need it.

questions.q: What is the difference between modules, plugins and collections?
questions.text: Modules run on targets and do the work. Plugins run on the control node and extend connections, lookups, filters and callbacks. Collections package modules, plugins and roles under a namespace and are versioned and pinned in requirements.yml. ansible-doc -t module ansible.builtin.copy ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml Interview tip: Say modules run on targets, plugins on the controller.

questions.q: What is the difference between ansible-core and the Ansible community package, and how do you manage versions?
questions.text: Ansible-core is the engine and built-ins; the community package adds many collections. Pin ansible-core and collection versions, ideally in an execution environment image, and test upgrades with lint and Molecule before rollout. pip install 'ansible-core==2.17.*' ansible-galaxy collection list Interview tip: Say pin versions and package them in an execution environment.

questions.q: Describe the structure of a playbook, plays and tasks.
questions.text: A playbook is a list of plays; each play targets hosts, sets options and runs pre_tasks, roles, tasks and post_tasks in order. Tasks call modules, run across hosts in parallel, and notify handlers. Keep plays short and named. - name: Configure web hosts: web become: true tasks: - name: Install nginx ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present Interview tip: Say name every task and push logic into roles.

questions.q: How do handlers work and what are the pitfalls?
questions.text: Handlers run once at the end of a play when notified by changed tasks, in definition order. Use meta flush_handlers to run earlier, force_handlers to run after failures, and listen to group handlers. - name: Update config ansible.builtin.template: src: app.conf.j2 dest: /etc/app.conf notify: Restart app - ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers Interview tip: Mention flush_handlers and the failed-play pitfall.

questions.q: How do loops work in Ansible, and when should you avoid them?
questions.text: Use loop with item, loop_control for labels and renamed variables, dict2items for dictionaries. Avoid loops where a module accepts a list, such as package, since one call is faster than many. - name: Create users ansible.builtin.user: name: "{{ item.name }}" groups: "{{ item.groups }}" loop: "{{ users }}" loop_control: label: "{{ item.name }}" Interview tip: Say pass a list to the module instead of looping where possible.

questions.q: How do conditionals with when and failed_when and changed_when work?
questions.text: when runs a task on a true expression; failed_when and changed_when redefine failure and change for tasks such as command. Use defaults for undefined variables and watch for string versus boolean types. - ansible.builtin.command: /usr/local/bin/check_app register: r failed_when: "'CRITICAL' in r.stdout" changed_when: false Interview tip: Say changed_when false for read-only commands.

questions.q: How do you handle errors with block, rescue and always, and ignore_errors?
questions.text: block groups tasks; rescue handles failures and always runs regardless, like try, catch and finally. Prefer this and targeted failed_when over ignore_errors, and use any_errors_fatal or max_fail_percentage for rolling changes. - block: - ansible.builtin.include_role: {name: deploy} rescue: - ansible.builtin.include_role: {name: rollback} always: - ansible.builtin.debug: {msg: "done"} Interview tip: Say rescue for rollback, always for cleanup.

questions.q: How are tags used, and what are the best practices?
questions.text: Tags let you run or skip subsets with --tags and --skip-tags. Imports inherit tags, dynamic includes need apply. Keep a small documented tag vocabulary and rely on full runs in CI. ansible-playbook site.yml --tags config --skip-tags deploy ansible-playbook site.yml --list-tags Interview tip: Mention the import versus include difference.

questions.q: What do delegate_to, run_once and local_action do, and when do you use them?
questions.text: delegate_to runs a task on another host while keeping the current host's variables, for load balancer, DNS or monitoring calls. run_once executes a task once per play or batch. Watch serial interactions and delegated credentials. - name: Drain from LB ansible.builtin.uri: url: "https://lb/api/drain/{{ inventory_hostname }}" method: POST delegate_to: localhost Interview tip: Say run_once applies per serial batch.

questions.q: How do check mode and diff mode work, and what are their limits?
questions.text: Check mode simulates changes and diff mode shows file differences, giving a reviewable dry run. Limits include modules without support, skipped command tasks and dependent tasks, so treat it as a signal, not a guarantee. ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff -l staging - ansible.builtin.command: cat /etc/app.conf check_mode: false changed_when: false Interview tip: Say dry-run is advisory; staging remains the proof.

questions.q: What is the difference between command, shell, raw and script modules?
questions.text: command runs without a shell and is safer; shell allows pipes but risks injection; raw needs no Python and suits bootstrapping; script copies and runs a local script. Prefer proper modules and make these idempotent with creates, removes and changed_when. - ansible.builtin.command: /opt/app/migrate args: creates: /var/lib/app/.migrated - ansible.builtin.shell: "ps aux | grep {{ name | quote }}" Interview tip: Say a module first, then command, shell last.

questions.q: What is the difference between include and import for tasks and roles?
questions.text: Import is static, processed at parse time, applying tags and conditions to inner tasks. Include is dynamic, evaluated at run time, so it supports loops and variable file names. Use imports for fixed structure and includes for runtime decisions. - ansible.builtin.import_tasks: common.yml - ansible.builtin.include_tasks: "{{ ansible_os_family }}.yml" Interview tip: Say static for structure, dynamic for runtime choices.

questions.q: What is the structure of an Ansible role and why use roles?
questions.text: A role has tasks, handlers, defaults, vars, templates, files and meta. It packages one capability for reuse and isolated testing. Keep one responsibility, document variables, prefix names and put overridable values in defaults. ansible-galaxy role init nginx tree roles/nginx Interview tip: Say prefix variables to avoid collisions.

questions.q: How do role dependencies work and what are their pitfalls?
questions.text: Dependencies in meta main run before a role and execute once by default unless allow_duplicates is set. They hide coupling and affect variable precedence, so keep them minimal and often compose roles explicitly in the playbook. # roles/app/meta/main.yml dependencies: - role: common - role: nginx vars: nginx_port: 8080 Interview tip: Say explicit composition is clearer than hidden dependencies.

questions.q: What are Ansible collections and how do you use and publish them?
questions.text: A collection bundles modules, plugins and roles under a namespace and version. Install from Galaxy or a private hub via requirements.yml, call by fully qualified name, and publish with galaxy.yml, ansible-galaxy build and publish, with ansible-test in CI. ansible-galaxy collection init myorg.platform ansible-galaxy collection build && ansible-galaxy collection publish myorg-platform-1.2.0.tar.gz Interview tip: Say semantic versions and a pinned requirements file.

questions.q: How do you use Galaxy and requirements.yml to manage dependencies reproducibly?
questions.text: requirements.yml pins the roles and collections a project needs. Install into a project-local path, pin versions or commits, use a private mirror, and reuse the file to build execution environment images so every environment matches. ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml -p ./roles collections: - name: kubernetes.core version: ">=3.0,<4.0" Interview tip: Say pin versions and mirror privately for reproducibility.

questions.q: When should logic be a role, a collection or a custom module?
questions.text: Use a role for reusable task sequences, a collection to package and version related content, and a custom module when you need real logic, an uncovered API, or proper idempotency and check mode. Search existing collections first. ansible-doc -l | grep -i grafana ansible-test sanity --docker default Interview tip: Say look for an existing module before writing one.

questions.q: Why use fully qualified collection names, and how do you migrate old playbooks?
questions.text: FQCNs such as ansible.builtin.copy remove ambiguity and shadowing risk and show which collection is required. Migrate with ansible-lint fqcn rule, add collections to requirements.yml and test in staging. ansible-lint --fix=fqcn site.yml ansible-doc ansible.builtin.service Interview tip: Say lint can auto-fix most short names.

questions.q: How do you write a custom Ansible module, and what makes it good?
questions.text: Write a Python file using AnsibleModule with an argument spec, compute current versus desired state, return exit_json with changed, support check mode, use no_log for secrets, and document with DOCUMENTATION, EXAMPLES and RETURN. Test with ansible-test. module = AnsibleModule(argument_spec=dict(name=dict(type='str', required=True)), supports_check_mode=True) module.exit_json(changed=changed, msg='ok') Interview tip: Say idempotent, check-mode aware and documented.

questions.q: What is the difference between role defaults and role vars, and how should you design role variables?
questions.text: Defaults are lowest precedence and form the role's public, overridable interface. Vars are high precedence internals such as per-OS package names. Prefix names, document defaults and validate inputs with assert or an argument spec. # roles/nginx/defaults/main.yml nginx_worker_processes: auto nginx_port: 80 - ansible.builtin.assert: that: nginx_port | int > 0 Interview tip: Say defaults are the API, vars are the internals.

questions.q: How do you write custom filter and lookup plugins, and when are they worthwhile?
questions.text: A filter plugin is a Python class mapping names to functions used in Jinja2; a lookup plugin returns data from the control node. Use them to replace repeated or unreadable template logic, keep them small, tested and documented. class FilterModule(object): def filters(self): return {'cidr_hosts': cidr_hosts} {{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'HOME') }} Interview tip: Say lookups run on the controller, not on the target.

questions.q: What are the ways to apply a role, and how do roles, import_role and include_role differ?
questions.text: The roles keyword applies roles statically before tasks; import_role is static anywhere in tasks; include_role is dynamic with loops and runtime names. Use public true to expose its variables. - ansible.builtin.include_role: name: "{{ item }}" loop: "{{ enabled_roles }}" - hosts: web roles: [common, nginx] Interview tip: Say choose static for predictability, dynamic for runtime decisions.

questions.q: Explain Ansible variable precedence and how to avoid surprises.
questions.text: Variables merge from defaults, inventory, group and host vars, facts, play vars, role vars, task vars, set_fact and extra vars, with more specific and explicit sources winning. Keep variables in few places, prefix names and debug with ansible-inventory and the debug module. ansible-inventory -i inventory --host web01 ansible web01 -m debug -a 'var=nginx_port' -i inventory Interview tip: Say defaults for knobs, group_vars for environments, extra vars for exceptions.

questions.q: How do you organise group_vars and host_vars for multiple environments?
questions.text: Use one inventory directory per environment with group_vars and host_vars, a group directory with vars.yml and vault.yml, shared values in an all group, and avoid deep hierarchies where precedence is fragile. inventories/ production/ hosts.yml group_vars/all/vars.yml group_vars/db/vault.yml staging/ ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml Interview tip: Say separate plain and vault files per group.

questions.q: How do Jinja2 templates work in Ansible and what are good practices?
questions.text: The template module renders Jinja2 on the controller with host variables. Keep logic simple, add an ansible_managed header, use validate before replacing, set mode and owner, use defaults and mandatory deliberately, and avoid exposing secrets. - ansible.builtin.template: src: nginx.conf.j2 dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf mode: '0644' validate: 'nginx -t -c %s' Interview tip: Say validate and ansible_managed.

questions.q: Which Jinja2 filters do you use most in Ansible, and for what?
questions.text: Key filters: default and mandatory, map, select, selectattr, join, unique, combine, dict2items, json_query, regex_replace, quote and type conversions. Keep chains short and move complex logic into set_fact or a custom filter. {{ users | selectattr('active') | map(attribute='name') | list }} {{ defaults | combine(overrides, recursive=True) }} Interview tip: Say default, mandatory, combine and selectattr are the workhorses.

questions.q: How do register, set_fact and magic variables like hostvars work together?
questions.text: register captures task output, set_fact defines run-time variables per host, and magic variables like hostvars, groups and inventory_hostname expose inventory and other hosts. Beware hostvars before facts are gathered, set_fact precedence and skipped registered results. - ansible.builtin.command: hostname -f register: fqdn - ansible.builtin.set_fact: db_host: "{{ hostvars[groups['db'][0]].ansible_default_ipv4.address }}" Interview tip: Say hostvars needs facts already gathered for that host.

questions.q: What are lookup plugins and how do you use them safely?
questions.text: Lookups fetch data on the control node from files, env, URLs, DNS or secret stores. Use query for lists, protect output with no_log, and evaluate expensive lookups once with set_fact. Remember paths are controller paths. {{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'files/key.pub') }} {{ lookup('community.hashi_vault.hashi_vault', 'secret/data/app:password') }} Interview tip: Say lookups run on the controller and should be no_log when secret.

questions.q: How do you generate configuration from structured data using loops in templates?
questions.text: Model data as YAML, loop in Jinja2 with loop.first and loop.last helpers, prepare data with filters or combine, and use task-level loops for one-file-per-item cases. Validate generated files with the service's checker. {% for v in vhosts %} server_name {{ v.name }}; {% endfor %} - ansible.builtin.template: src: vhost.j2 dest: "/etc/nginx/conf.d/{{ item.name }}.conf" loop: "{{ vhosts }}" Interview tip: Say separate the data model from the template.

questions.q: How do you merge default and override dictionaries, and what are the pitfalls?
questions.text: Use combine, with recursive true for nested dictionaries and list_merge to control lists. Keep defaults and overrides as separate variables, and avoid global hash_behaviour merge since precedence otherwise replaces whole dictionaries. {{ app_defaults | combine(app_overrides | default({}), recursive=True, list_merge='append') }} Interview tip: Say variables replace by default, so combine explicitly.

questions.q: What is Ansible Vault and how do you use it?
questions.text: Vault encrypts files or single strings with AES-256 so secrets can live in git. Supply the password through a file or script, keep encrypted variables in a separate vault.yml referenced by plain names, rekey to rotate, and consider an external secrets manager at scale. ansible-vault encrypt group_vars/prod/vault.yml ansible-vault encrypt_string 's3cr3t' --name 'db_password' ansible-playbook site.yml --vault-password-file ~/.vault_pass Interview tip: Say never commit the password file.

questions.q: How do vault IDs work and how do you use multiple vault passwords?
questions.text: Vault IDs label encrypted content, so different environments use different passwords. Provide several vault-id sources at run time; Ansible matches the label. Use scripts to fetch passwords from a secrets manager and limit who holds the production one. ansible-vault encrypt --vault-id prod@prompt group_vars/prod/vault.yml ansible-playbook site.yml --vault-id dev@~/.vault_dev --vault-id prod@scripts/get_prod_pass.sh Interview tip: Say the label is not a security boundary; password access is.

questions.q: How do you integrate Ansible with HashiCorp Vault or cloud secret managers instead of using Ansible Vault?
questions.text: Use lookup plugins for HashiCorp Vault, AWS, Azure or GCP secret managers, authenticate with short-lived identities such as AppRole, OIDC or instance identity, set no_log, and in AWX use external credential sources so secrets are not stored in job templates. {{ lookup('amazon.aws.aws_secret', 'prod/db/password', region='us-east-1') }} vault write auth/approle/login role_id=$ROLE secret_id=$SECRET Interview tip: Say no static tokens and no_log on the task.

questions.q: What does no_log do, and how else do you keep secrets out of logs and output?
questions.text: no_log hides task arguments and results from output and logs. Use it only where needed, avoid command-line secrets, disable diff on secret templates, mask CI variables and avoid printing registered results. - ansible.builtin.uri: url: https://api/login body: {password: "{{ api_pass }}"} no_log: true - ansible.builtin.template: src: secrets.j2 dest: /etc/app/secrets diff: false Interview tip: Say no_log hides debugging too, so scope it.

questions.q: How do you secure SSH access and key management for Ansible?
questions.text: Use a dedicated automation account with key-only auth, per-environment keys or short-lived SSH certificates, restricted sudo, host key checking enabled and a hardened, audited bastion for private networks. ansible_ssh_common_args='-o ProxyJump=bastion' ssh-keygen -s ca_key -I ansible-ctl -n ansible -V +1h id_ed25519.pub Interview tip: Say short-lived SSH certificates beat long-lived keys.

questions.q: How do you use Ansible for security hardening and compliance, such as CIS benchmarks?
questions.text: Start from maintained hardening roles, make controls tagged and toggleable with documented exceptions, assess in check mode, apply in stages with a canary group, verify with OpenSCAP or InSpec, and schedule runs to catch drift. ansible-galaxy collection install devsec.hardening ansible-playbook harden.yml --check --diff -l canary Interview tip: Say staged rollout, verification scan and exceptions with reasons.

questions.q: How do you design privilege escalation and sudo policy for automation accounts?
questions.text: Use dedicated automation accounts with key login and sudoers entries validated by visudo. Prefer command-limited sudo where practical, protect the controller strongly if root is needed, apply become only to needed tasks and audit sudo activity. - ansible.builtin.copy: dest: /etc/sudoers.d/ansible content: "ansible ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart app\n" validate: 'visudo -cf %s' mode: '0440' Interview tip: Say the controller becomes the crown jewel if sudo is broad.

questions.q: How do you handle secrets in CI/CD pipelines that run Ansible?
questions.text: Keep secrets in the CI secret store scoped to protected branches, prefer OIDC to fetch short-lived credentials, write vault passwords to temporary files and remove them, load SSH keys into an agent only per job, mask logs and require approval for production. echo "$VAULT_PASS" > .vp && chmod 600 .vp && ansible-playbook site.yml --vault-password-file .vp; rm -f .vp ssh-add - <<< "$DEPLOY_KEY" Interview tip: Say OIDC short-lived credentials beat stored secrets.

questions.q: How do you audit and review Ansible code for security problems?
questions.text: Run ansible-lint with a strict profile and secret scanning in CI, review privilege, downloads, disabled validation and secrets, protect production branches, keep AWX audit logs centrally, and pin and mirror third-party roles and collections. ansible-lint --profile production gitleaks detect --source . Interview tip: Say pin and mirror third-party content.

questions.q: How do extra vars, vars_files and include_vars differ, and when do you use each?
questions.text: Extra vars have the highest precedence and suit run-time parameters; vars_files loads fixed files at play start; include_vars loads dynamically, for example per OS with first_found. Convert types and restrict inputs in AWX surveys. ansible-playbook deploy.yml -e version=1.4.2 -e @env/prod.yml - ansible.builtin.include_vars: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.first_found', ['{{ ansible_distribution }}.yml','default.yml']) }}" Interview tip: Say extra vars for parameters, not for configuration.

questions.q: How do you validate inputs and variables so a playbook fails early with clear messages?
questions.text: Use assert with clear messages, the mandatory filter, role argument_specs for typed validation, AWX surveys and pre-flight tasks for connectivity and capacity, so a bad input fails before any change. - ansible.builtin.assert: that: - app_version is match('^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$') - app_port | int in range(1024, 65536) fail_msg: 'Invalid app_version or app_port' Interview tip: Say fail early with a human-readable message.

questions.q: How do you rotate secrets and the vault password with minimal disruption?
questions.text: Rekey vault files with ansible-vault rekey, rotate per vault ID, update pipeline secrets and revoke the old password after an overlap. For application secrets, rotate at the source, support two credentials during transition and consider a secrets manager with dynamic credentials. ansible-vault rekey --vault-id prod@old_pass --new-vault-id prod@new_pass group_vars/prod/vault.yml grep -rl '$ANSIBLE_VAULT' . | xargs ansible-vault rekey --new-vault-password-file new_pass Interview tip: Say plan an overlap, then revoke the old secret.

questions.q: How do forks affect performance, and how do you tune them?
questions.text: Forks sets parallel hosts per task, default five. Raise it stepwise while watching controller CPU, memory and bastion limits, remember serial caps batch size, and for very large fleets spread work across multiple execution nodes. ansible-playbook site.yml -f 50 [defaults] forks = 50 Interview tip: Say measure, increase gradually and watch the controller.

questions.q: What are the linear, free and other strategies, and when do you use them?
questions.text: Linear keeps hosts in lockstep and is predictable; free lets each host run ahead for speed when tasks are independent; host_pinned and debug are variants. Use linear for coordinated changes and free for independent bulk work. - hosts: all strategy: free tasks: [] ANSIBLE_STRATEGY=linux ansible-playbook site.yml Interview tip: Say free is faster but loses ordering guarantees.

questions.q: How do you do rolling updates with serial, and control failures during them?
questions.text: serial limits a play to batches, which gives rolling updates and canary patterns with a growing list. Add max_fail_percentage or any_errors_fatal and health checks so a failing batch stops the rollout; keep enough capacity while batches are out. - hosts: web serial: [1, 5, '25%'] max_fail_percentage: 10 tasks: [] Interview tip: Say canary first batch plus health checks and a failure threshold.

questions.q: How do SSH pipelining, ControlPersist and Mitogen speed up Ansible?
questions.text: ControlPersist reuses SSH connections and pipelining sends modules over the existing session, cutting round trips, provided requiretty is off. Mitogen can speed things further but has compatibility trade-offs. Measure with profile_tasks. [ssh_connection] pipelining = True ssh_args = -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=60s ANSIBLE_CALLBACKS_ENABLED=ansible.posix.profile_tasks ansible-playbook site.yml Interview tip: Say measure with profile_tasks before and after.

questions.q: How do fact caching and limiting fact gathering help at scale?
questions.text: Disable or subset fact gathering, and enable a fact cache such as Redis or JSON with smart gathering and a timeout so recent facts are reused. Watch staleness and refresh volatile facts explicitly. [defaults] gathering = smart fact_caching = redis fact_caching_timeout = 3600 fact_caching_connection = redis01:6379:0 Interview tip: Say pick a timeout matching how fast facts change.

questions.q: How do async and poll work, and when do you use them for long-running tasks?
questions.text: async sets a maximum run time and poll sets how often to check, avoiding connection timeouts; poll zero fires and forgets, and async_status collects results later in a retry loop. Handle failures when collecting. - ansible.builtin.command: /usr/local/bin/backup.sh async: 3600 poll: 0 register: job - ansible.builtin.async_status: jid: "{{ job.ansible_job_id }}" register: r until: r.finished retries: 60 delay: 30 Interview tip: Say poll 0 plus async_status lets tasks overlap.

questions.q: How do you manage very large or fast-changing inventories?
questions.text: Make the inventory a view over a source of truth with plugins, caching, keyed groups and filters, keep group structure shallow, put variables in groups, limit runs to slices, and spread work over several controllers or instance groups. ansible-inventory -i aws_ec2.yml --list --yaml | head plugin: amazon.aws.aws_ec2 cache: true cache_timeout: 300 keyed_groups: - key: tags.Role prefix: role Interview tip: Say the inventory is derived from truth, never hand-maintained.

questions.q: How would you patch thousands of Linux servers safely with Ansible?
questions.text: Group by criticality, pre-check capacity and backups, patch in serial batches starting with a canary, drain and return from the load balancer, reboot only when required, health-check each host, stop on a failure threshold and report results. - ansible.builtin.reboot: reboot_timeout: 900 when: reboot_required.stat.exists ansible-playbook patch.yml -l canary --check --diff Interview tip: Say canary, batch, health check, stop threshold.

questions.q: A host shows UNREACHABLE. How do you troubleshoot it?
questions.text: UNREACHABLE means no connection. Reproduce with the same SSH command using -vvv, then check address, DNS, firewall, user, key, host keys, sshd logs and bastion settings. Once SSH works manually, retest with the ping module. ansible web01 -m ping -vvvv ssh -vvv -i ~/.ssh/ansible ansible@10.0.1.12 Interview tip: Say replicate the exact SSH command with -vvvv first.

questions.q: A playbook is slow. How do you find out why and speed it up?
questions.text: Profile with profile_tasks to find the slowest tasks, then fix the cause: fact gathering, low forks, SSH overhead, per-item loops, repeated package cache updates, slow lookups or the linear strategy waiting on one host. Re-measure after each change. ANSIBLE_CALLBACKS_ENABLED=ansible.posix.profile_tasks,ansible.posix.timer ansible-playbook site.yml - ansible.builtin.apt: update_cache: true cache_valid_time: 3600 Interview tip: Say measure with profile_tasks, then change one thing at a time.

questions.q: How do you debug a failing playbook: verbosity, the debug module and the debugger?
questions.text: Raise verbosity with -v to -vvvv, use the debug module to inspect variables and results, use the debugger keyword or debug strategy for interactive failures, and use step, start-at-task, syntax-check, list-tasks and ansible-inventory --host to narrow down. ansible-playbook site.yml -vvv --start-at-task 'Install nginx' - hosts: web debugger: on_failed ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check Interview tip: Say -vvvv for connection issues and debugger for logic issues.

questions.q: A task reports changed on every run. How do you track it down?
questions.text: Always-changed tasks usually are command or shell without changed_when, unstable templates, regexes that do not match their own output, mode written as a number, or latest versions. Run twice with diff, fix, and add a CI check that the second run has zero changes. ansible-playbook site.yml --diff | grep -A5 'changed:' - ansible.builtin.file: path: /etc/app mode: '0755' Interview tip: Say quote file modes and use changed_when on commands.

questions.q: You get an 'undefined variable' error or a templating failure. What is your approach?
questions.text: Read the error for the variable and task, check where it should be defined, inspect with debug and ansible-inventory --host, and look for typos, wrong groups, skipped registers, missing facts, precedence or YAML quoting problems. Then fix with defaults, mandatory and early asserts. ansible web01 -m debug -a 'var=hostvars[inventory_hostname]' -i inventory ansible-inventory -i inventory --host web01 | jq . Interview tip: Say add an assert so the next failure is clearer.

questions.q: How do you troubleshoot privilege escalation failures, such as a missing sudo password?
questions.text: Reproduce with ssh and sudo -n true. Check sudoers entries, requiretty, the become method and variables, whether become_user can read temporary files (needs acl), and noisy shell profiles. Fix sudoers with visudo and set become settings explicitly. ssh ansible@host 'sudo -n true && echo ok' ansible web01 -m ping -b -vvv Interview tip: Say test sudo manually before touching Ansible.

questions.q: What causes 'module not found', Python interpreter and dependency errors on targets?
questions.text: Interpreter or library errors come from missing Python or packages on the host running the module, which for cloud modules is usually the controller. Set ansible_python_interpreter, install requirements in the right environment or execution environment, and install missing collections. ansible --version ansible newhost -m raw -a 'apt-get install -y python3' -b pip install boto3 botocore Interview tip: Say know which Python runs the module: controller or target.

questions.q: A handler did not run, or ran at the wrong time. Why?
questions.text: Handlers run only on a changed notify, after the play, in definition order. They can be skipped by earlier failures unless force_handlers is set, by name mismatches or by scope. Use flush_handlers for mid-play restarts and listen to decouple names. - hosts: web force_handlers: true tasks: - ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers Interview tip: Say changed is the trigger, and failures can skip handlers.

questions.q: A playbook fails to parse because of YAML or syntax errors. How do you find and avoid them?
questions.text: Run syntax-check, then yamllint and ansible-lint. Typical errors are indentation, unquoted colons or braces, yes and no becoming booleans, duplicate keys and numeric versions. Use editor schema validation, pre-commit hooks and quote strings. ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check yamllint . && ansible-lint Interview tip: Say quote versions and use true or false for booleans.

questions.q: Vault decryption fails with 'Decryption failed' or a missing password. How do you resolve it?
questions.text: Identify the file and vault ID, test with ansible-vault view, and check for wrong or missing password sources, mismatched labels, corrupted headers or an unattached AWX credential. Restore or rekey as needed, and add a CI check decrypting every vault file. ansible-vault view group_vars/prod/vault.yml --vault-id prod@scripts/get_pass.sh head -1 group_vars/prod/vault.yml Interview tip: Say test decryption alone with ansible-vault view.

questions.q: When would you use ansible-pull instead of the usual push model?
questions.text: ansible-pull makes each host fetch a Git repo and apply it locally on a schedule. It scales widely and suits NAT, edge and autoscaled hosts, but loses central orchestration and visibility, so combine it with push for coordinated changes. ansible-pull -U https://git.example.com/infra.git -i localhost, local.yml */15 * * * * root ansible-pull -o -U $REPO local.yml >> /var/log/ansible-pull.log Interview tip: Say pull for convergence at scale, push for orchestration.

questions.q: How do you protect rate-limited APIs and shared systems when automation runs in parallel?
questions.text: Use throttle to limit concurrent executions of a task, serial for batch size and forks for global parallelism, add retries with delay on throttling errors, use run_once for single calls, and mirror downloads to reduce external load. - ansible.builtin.uri: url: https://api.example.com/register throttle: 3 register: r until: r.status == 200 retries: 5 delay: 10 Interview tip: Say throttle protects the dependency, not the controller.

questions.q: What is the difference between AWX, Ansible Automation Platform and Ansible Tower?
questions.text: Tower was the original commercial product, AWX is the open source upstream, and AAP is Red Hat's supported platform with the automation controller, Automation Hub, execution environments, Event-Driven Ansible and mesh. The concepts transfer across all three. kubectl get awx -n awx curl -s -u admin:$PASS https://awx.example.com/api/v2/ping/ Interview tip: Say AWX is upstream, AAP is supported, same concepts.

questions.q: Explain projects, inventories, credentials and job templates in AWX or the controller.
questions.text: Projects pull playbooks from Git, inventories hold hosts, credentials store encrypted secrets injected at run time, and job templates combine them with variables, limits and options. Users get permission to run templates without seeing secrets. awx job_templates launch 12 --extra_vars '{"version":"1.4.2"}' --monitor awx projects update 5 --monitor Interview tip: Say delegated, audited execution without exposing secrets.

questions.q: How does role-based access control work in AWX and the automation controller?
questions.text: Organisations contain teams, users and resources; roles such as admin, execute, use and read are granted on objects, best through teams mapped from LDAP, SAML or OIDC. Apply least privilege, separate credentials per environment and audit via the activity stream. awx roles grant --team 3 --resource-type job_template --resource 12 --role execute awx teams list Interview tip: Say teams mapped from the identity provider.

questions.q: What are workflow templates in AWX and how do you use approvals and conditional paths?
questions.text: Workflows chain job templates, syncs and approval nodes with success, failure and always paths. Use set_stats to pass data, approvals for production gates and convergence for parallel branches, keeping complex logic in playbooks. - ansible.builtin.set_stats: data: build_id: "{{ build_id }}" per_host: false awx workflow_job_templates launch 7 --monitor Interview tip: Say approvals and rollback paths make a release workflow.

questions.q: What are execution environments and how do you build and manage them?
questions.text: An execution environment is a container image with ansible-core, collections and dependencies. Build with ansible-builder from a definition file, push to a registry, assign it to job templates, and use ansible-navigator locally for parity. Version, scan and rebuild regularly. ansible-builder build -t registry.example.com/ee-platform:1.3 -f execution-environment.yml ansible-navigator run site.yml --eei registry.example.com/ee-platform:1.3 -m stdout Interview tip: Say the EE makes laptop, CI and controller identical.

questions.q: How do instance groups and automation mesh help scale and isolate execution?
questions.text: Instance groups pool execution capacity, and automation mesh via Receptor links control, execution and hop nodes across networks. Place execution nodes near targets, bind inventories or templates to groups, scale by adding nodes, and use container groups for elastic per-job pods. awx instance_groups list kubectl get pods -n awx -l app.kubernetes.io/name=awx-task Interview tip: Say execution near the targets, control plane in the centre.

questions.q: How do you integrate AWX with CI/CD, webhooks, surveys and notifications?
questions.text: Use the REST API, awx CLI or collection to launch templates from CI, webhooks for repository events, surveys for validated self-service inputs, notification templates for results and schedules for recurring jobs. Use scoped OAuth tokens for service accounts. awx job_templates launch deploy-app --extra_vars '{"version":"1.4.2"}' --monitor --timeout 1800 curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://awx.example.com/api/v2/job_templates/12/launch/ Interview tip: Say a scoped service account token and validated surveys.

questions.q: How do you deploy, size and make AWX highly available on Kubernetes?
questions.text: Deploy with the AWX operator and an AWX custom resource, use an external highly available PostgreSQL, run multiple web and task replicas with anti-affinity, separate execution into container groups, size by forks and monitor queue times. kubectl apply -k github.com/ansible/awx-operator/config/default?ref=2.19.0 kubectl get awx,pods -n awx Interview tip: Say external database and separated execution capacity.

questions.q: What is Event-Driven Ansible and where does it fit?
questions.text: EDA runs automation in response to events through rulebooks with sources such as webhooks, Kafka or Alertmanager, rules that match conditions and actions that run playbooks. Restrict to safe idempotent remediations with rate limits, approvals and logging. ansible-rulebook --rulebook alerts.yml -i inventory.yml --verbose - name: restart on alert condition: event.alert.labels.alertname == 'ServiceDown' action: run_job_template: name: restart-service Interview tip: Say auto-remediation needs guardrails against loops.

questions.q: How do you back up, upgrade and recover the automation controller?
questions.text: Back up the database, projects and secrets including the credential encryption key, using AWXBackup or the installer and database PITR. Upgrade stepwise after a backup and verify with a test job. Keep controller configuration as code and test restores. kubectl apply -f awxbackup.yaml kubectl get awxbackup -n awx Interview tip: Say test the restore and keep config as code.

questions.q: How do you combine Terraform and Ansible in one workflow?
questions.text: Terraform creates infrastructure and Ansible configures it. Hand off through a tag-based dynamic inventory or the cloud.terraform inventory plugin, in a pipeline of Terraform apply, wait for connectivity, then Ansible. Prefer pipelines to provisioners. terraform apply -auto-approve && ansible-playbook -i terraform.yml configure.yml plugin: cloud.terraform.terraform_provider project_path: ./infra Interview tip: Say tags from Terraform drive the Ansible inventory.

questions.q: How do you use Ansible with AWS: dynamic inventory, SSM and common modules?
questions.text: Use amazon.aws with the aws_ec2 inventory plugin and tag-based groups, authenticate with roles or OIDC, and use the aws_ssm connection for access without inbound ports or keys. Install boto3 in the controller environment, and use Terraform for lifecycle at scale. ansible-inventory -i aws_ec2.yml --graph ansible_connection: community.aws.aws_ssm ansible_aws_ssm_bucket_name: ansible-ssm-transfer Interview tip: Say SSM removes SSH keys and inbound ports.

questions.q: How do you manage Kubernetes resources with Ansible, and when is it appropriate?
questions.text: kubernetes.core provides k8s, k8s_info and helm modules. Use Ansible for cluster bootstrap, namespaces, RBAC, base charts and cross-system orchestration, and GitOps controllers for continuous reconciliation of applications. Use wait conditions in playbooks. - kubernetes.core.k8s: state: present src: manifests/namespace.yaml apply: true wait: true pip install kubernetes Interview tip: Say Ansible bootstraps clusters; GitOps reconciles apps.

questions.q: How is Ansible used for network device automation?
questions.text: Vendor collections provide network modules over network_cli, netconf or httpapi from the controller. Prefer idempotent resource modules with states like merged and replaced, back up configs first, template from data models, check and roll out gradually. - cisco.ios.ios_vlans: config: - vlan_id: 100 name: app state: merged - cisco.ios.ios_config: backup: true Interview tip: Say resource modules with states, plus a config backup first.

questions.q: How do you manage Windows hosts with Ansible?
questions.text: Use WinRM over HTTPS or SSH with the ansible.windows collections, Kerberos for domain hosts, dedicated modules for idempotency, win_reboot for restarts and become runas for elevation. Watch for firewall, time skew and double-hop issues. ansible_connection: winrm ansible_winrm_transport: kerberos ansible_port: 5986 - ansible.windows.win_feature: name: Web-Server state: present Interview tip: Say Kerberos over HTTPS and real modules, not win_shell.

questions.q: How do you use Ansible to configure OpenStack or VMware infrastructure and virtual machines?
questions.text: Use openstack.cloud with clouds.yaml, and community.vmware for vCenter, for provisioning, snapshots and operations, with inventory plugins for dynamic groups. Prefer Terraform for long-lived resource state and Ansible for in-guest configuration. Install SDKs and handle waits and tags. - openstack.cloud.server: cloud: prod name: app01 image: ubuntu-22.04 flavor: m1.medium network: tenant-net wait: true ansible-galaxy collection install openstack.cloud community.vmware Interview tip: Say Ansible configures the guest, Terraform holds lifecycle state.

questions.q: How do you build golden images with Packer and Ansible?
questions.text: Packer launches a build instance, runs an Ansible playbook with its provisioner, cleans secrets and caches and saves the image. Reuse roles, test with InSpec or Testinfra, version and scan images and rebuild regularly for patches. provisioner "ansible" { playbook_file = "playbooks/baseline.yml" } packer build -var-file=prod.pkrvars.hcl image.pkr.hcl Interview tip: Say bake once, replace instead of patching.

questions.q: How do you deploy and configure monitoring and logging agents consistently across a fleet?
questions.text: Create a role per agent with pinned, checksummed downloads, a dedicated user, systemd unit, templated config, handlers and a health check, apply by inventory group, keep secrets in vault, generate scrape targets from inventory and roll out in batches. - ansible.builtin.uri: url: http://localhost:9100/metrics status_code: 200 retries: 5 delay: 3 - ansible.builtin.get_url: url: "{{ node_exporter_url }}" checksum: "sha256:{{ node_exporter_sha }}" dest: /tmp/ne.tgz Interview tip: Say verify the agent after install and roll out in batches.

questions.q: How would you automate a zero-downtime application deployment with Ansible?
questions.text: Use serial batches, drain each host from the load balancer with a delegated task, deploy a versioned release and switch a symlink or image, run migrations once, wait for health checks, return the host, and use rescue for rollback with a canary first batch. - ansible.builtin.file: src: "/opt/app/releases/{{ version }}" dest: /opt/app/current state: link - ansible.builtin.uri: url: http://localhost:8080/health register: h until: h.status == 200 retries: 20 delay: 3 Interview tip: Say drain, deploy, health check, return, with a rollback path.

questions.q: When would you choose Ansible over Helm, Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools?
questions.text: Use Helm, operators and GitOps controllers for continuous reconciliation of in-cluster applications. Use Ansible for node OS, cluster bootstrap, network devices, databases and ordered multi-system procedures, often handing off to GitOps after bootstrap. ansible-playbook bootstrap-cluster.yml kubectl -n argocd get applications Interview tip: Say Ansible for the outside and orchestration, GitOps for in-cluster state.

questions.q: How do you use ansible-lint and what does it catch?
questions.text: ansible-lint catches style, naming, FQCN, risky command and shell use, missing changed_when, permissions, deprecated syntax and secret handling issues. Choose a profile, auto-fix where possible, run it in pre-commit and CI, and document any skipped rules. ansible-lint --profile production playbooks/ ansible-lint --fix Interview tip: Say adopt profiles progressively and make it a required CI check.

questions.q: How does Molecule test Ansible roles, and what does a good test cover?
questions.text: Molecule runs scenarios that create disposable platforms, converge the role, check idempotence, verify with Ansible assertions, Testinfra or InSpec and destroy. Test the OS matrix, variable combinations, upgrades and failure paths, and run it in CI. molecule init scenario default -r nginx -d podman molecule test Interview tip: Say the idempotence step makes the check automatic.

questions.q: What does a CI/CD pipeline for Ansible code look like?
questions.text: On pull requests run lint, syntax checks, Molecule, secret scans and check mode with diff against staging. After merge deploy to staging, smoke test, then promote the same revision to production behind approval via the controller, with branch protection and separate credentials. ansible-lint && ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging site.yml --check --diff Interview tip: Say promote the same revision through environments.

questions.q: How do you structure an Ansible repository for multiple teams and environments?
questions.text: Use a top-level config and requirements, an inventory directory per environment with group_vars, thin playbooks, logic in roles or versioned collections, and environment differences only in variables. Use CODEOWNERS and conventions, and split into repos when teams need independent releases. tree -L 2 . ├── ansible.cfg ├── requirements.yml ├── inventories/{prod,staging} ├── playbooks/ └── collections/ git log --oneline -- roles/nginx Interview tip: Say one code base, environment differences in inventory only.

questions.q: How do you build and use ansible-navigator and a local development workflow that matches production?
questions.text: Build an execution environment, run locally with ansible-navigator against it, reuse the same image in CI and the controller, add pre-commit lint and Molecule, and record the image tag in the repository. ansible-navigator run site.yml -i inventories/staging --eei registry.example.com/ee-platform:1.3 --mode stdout ansible-navigator replay artifact.json Interview tip: Say the same image everywhere removes drift.

questions.q: How do you promote changes across environments and roll back safely?
questions.text: Promote one revision through environments by changing only the inventory, with approvals in production. Prepare rollback with previous tags, release directories and symlinks, rescue blocks and snapshots, rehearse it in staging and record the revision per run. git checkout v1.4.1 && ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod deploy.yml -e version=1.4.1 ansible-playbook rollback.yml --tags rollback Interview tip: Say rehearse the rollback; untested rollbacks fail.

questions.q: How do you detect and handle configuration drift with Ansible?
questions.text: Schedule check-mode and diff runs from the controller and report any would-change tasks as drift. Keep roles idempotent to avoid noise, auto-enforce low-risk settings, review drift on sensitive systems, and reduce manual changes through access control. ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff -i inventories/prod | tee drift-$(date +%F).log awx job_templates launch drift-check --monitor Interview tip: Say drift reports need idempotent roles to be trustworthy.

questions.q: How do you migrate shell scripts and manual runbooks into Ansible?
questions.text: Inventory what the script does, replace commands with state-based modules, wrap leftovers with creates and changed_when, move values to variables and secrets to vault, test equivalence in staging, add tests and review, run through the controller and retire the script. ansible-playbook migrate.yml --check --diff -l test01 diff <(ssh old 'rpm -qa | sort') <(ssh new 'rpm -qa | sort') Interview tip: Say compare end states, then retire the script.

questions.q: How do you test playbooks end to end, beyond role-level Molecule tests?
questions.text: Create an ephemeral production-like environment, apply the full playbook against a mirrored inventory, verify with assertions, Testinfra, InSpec or Goss and a smoke test, re-run to check idempotence, test risky procedures, destroy the environment and keep artifacts. ansible-playbook -i inventories/ci site.yml && ansible-playbook -i inventories/ci site.yml | grep -q 'changed=0' goss -g goss.yaml validate Interview tip: Say test the whole playbook, not just the roles.

questions.q: How do you version, release and document roles and collections for other teams?
questions.text: Use semantic versions, changelog fragments, tagged releases built and published to a private hub by the pipeline, version-range pinning by consumers, a deprecation policy, documentation in READMEs and argument specs, and clear ownership. antsibull-changelog release --version 1.3.0 ansible-galaxy collection build && ansible-galaxy collection publish *.tar.gz --server private_hub Interview tip: Say semver, changelog, pinned consumers, deprecation notice.

questions.q: Which Ansible command-line tools do you use besides ansible-playbook, and what does each do?
questions.text: Use ansible-doc for offline module help, ansible-inventory to verify parsed inventory, ansible-config dump for effective settings, ansible-galaxy for dependencies, ansible-vault for secrets, ansible-console for interactive runs, and ansible-lint before committing. ansible-doc -s ansible.builtin.copy ansible-inventory -i inventory --graph --vars ansible-config dump --only-changed Interview tip: Say inspect first with inventory and config, then run.

questions.q: What YAML pitfalls commonly break Ansible playbooks?
questions.text: Use spaces only, quote booleans-like words, versions, file modes and anything starting with a brace or containing a colon-space, use pipe or greater-than for multi-line text, avoid duplicate keys, and run yamllint, ansible-lint and syntax-check. mode: "0644" version: "1.10" ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check && yamllint . Interview tip: Say quote modes, versions and anything brace-leading.

questions.q: How does Ansible pick and use the Python interpreter on managed hosts?
questions.text: Ansible auto-discovers the target Python; for minimal images or special libraries set ansible_python_interpreter explicitly in inventory, bootstrap Python with the raw module on bare hosts, and use a virtualenv when modules need extra packages. ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3 ansible bare -m raw -a 'apt-get install -y python3' -b Interview tip: Say pin the interpreter in group vars.

questions.q: What happens under the hood when Ansible runs a task on a remote host?
questions.text: The controller templates arguments, bundles the module, copies it to a temp directory over SSH, runs it with Python, reads the JSON result, then cleans up; pipelining streams the module to avoid the copy. The controller does all the logic. ansible all -m ping -vvv ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1 ansible web -m setup Interview tip: Say module copy, execute, JSON back, cleanup.

questions.q: What conventions make an Ansible playbook readable and maintainable?
questions.text: Name every task, use fully qualified module names, prefer dedicated modules, keep tasks single-purpose, prefix role variables, keep secrets out, put logic in roles and templates, keep playbooks thin, and enforce style with ansible-lint and yamllint. - name: Ensure nginx is installed ansible.builtin.package: name: nginx state: present ansible-lint --profile production Interview tip: Say names, FQCN, one thing per task, lint in CI.

questions.q: How do you use until, retries and wait_for to handle tasks that need time to succeed?
questions.text: Use wait_for for ports and files, and until with retries and delay for polling APIs; set realistic timeouts, let the final failure stop the play, and avoid fixed pauses. Combine with serial so each batch must be healthy first. - ansible.builtin.uri: url: http://localhost:8080/health register: r until: r.status == 200 retries: 20 delay: 5 - ansible.builtin.wait_for: port: 8080 timeout: 120 Interview tip: Say poll for readiness, never sleep blindly.

questions.q: How do you control loop output and iterate over complex data structures?
questions.text: Use loop_control with label for quiet output, loop_var to avoid collisions, pause for rate limits, dict2items for mappings and subelements for nested lists; pass whole lists to modules that accept them instead of looping. loop: "{{ users }}" loop_control: label: "{{ item.name }}" loop_var: user loop: "{{ app_config | dict2items }}" Interview tip: Say label your loops and rename loop_var in includes.

questions.q: How do any_errors_fatal and max_fail_percentage protect a rolling operation?
questions.text: By default failed hosts drop out while others continue. any_errors_fatal stops the whole play on any failure; max_fail_percentage with serial aborts a rollout when too many hosts in a batch fail. Use a canary batch and health checks. - hosts: web serial: [1, 5, 25%] max_fail_percentage: 10 any_errors_fatal: false Interview tip: Say bad releases should stop after the first batch.

questions.q: What are meta tasks and when do you use flush_handlers, end_play, end_host and refresh_inventory?
questions.text: Meta tasks steer the run: flush_handlers applies pending handlers now, end_play and end_host exit early, refresh_inventory reloads hosts created mid-run. Use sparingly and explain why. - ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers - ansible.builtin.meta: refresh_inventory Interview tip: Say flush handlers before health checks.

questions.q: How do you develop and debug playbooks efficiently with start-at-task, step, list-tasks and limit?
questions.text: Use --list-tasks and --list-hosts to preview, --limit for a canary host, --tags to select tasks, --start-at-task and --step during development, and check and diff for dry runs. Re-run failed hosts with a limit; avoid start-at-task in pipelines. ansible-playbook site.yml --list-tasks --limit web01 ansible-playbook site.yml --limit web01 --step --diff Interview tip: Say test on one host before the fleet.

questions.q: What are argument_specs and how do they validate role inputs?
questions.text: Argument specs in meta/argument_specs.yml declare variable types, defaults, choices and required flags per entry point; Ansible validates inputs before tasks run and the file doubles as documentation. Use assert for cross-field rules. argument_specs: main: options: nginx_port: type: int default: 80 nginx_state: choices: [present, absent] required: true Interview tip: Say fail early with a clear message.

questions.q: How do you design a role that works across several operating systems?
questions.text: Load per-distribution or family variable files with a first-found lookup for packages, services and paths, keep tasks generic with package and service modules, isolate truly different logic in per-family task files, and test each platform with Molecule. - ansible.builtin.include_vars: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.first_found', params) }}" vars: params: files: - "{{ ansible_distribution }}-{{ ansible_distribution_major_version }}.yml" - "{{ ansible_os_family }}.yml" - default.yml paths: [vars] Interview tip: Say variables per OS, tasks generic.

questions.q: When do you use template, copy, lineinfile, blockinfile and replace for managing files?
questions.text: Use template for files you fully own, copy for static content, lineinfile and blockinfile for small edits to shared files, and replace for regex substitutions. Prefer drop-in conf.d files and always use validate so bad configs are never activated. - ansible.builtin.template: src: app.conf.j2 dest: /etc/app/conf.d/10-app.conf validate: '/usr/sbin/app --check %s' - ansible.builtin.lineinfile: path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-tune.conf line: 'vm.swappiness=10' create: true Interview tip: Say own the whole file when you can; validate always.

questions.q: How do you manage users, groups, SSH keys and sudoers with Ansible safely?
questions.text: Describe users in variables, use user, group and authorized_key with exclusive, write sudo drop-ins validated with visudo, hash any passwords and keep them in vault, remove accounts explicitly, and prefer central identity with reviewed changes. - ansible.builtin.copy: dest: /etc/sudoers.d/ops content: '%ops ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl' mode: '0440' validate: 'visudo -cf %s' Interview tip: Say always validate sudoers before activating.

questions.q: How do you make roles idempotent and safe in check mode?
questions.text: Use declarative modules, guard command and shell with creates, removes and accurate changed_when, avoid always-changing templates, restart through handlers, set check_mode false on read-only discovery tasks, and enforce a no-change second run with Molecule. - ansible.builtin.command: /opt/app/init.sh args: creates: /var/lib/app/.initialised - ansible.builtin.command: app status register: st changed_when: false check_mode: false Interview tip: Say second run must change nothing.

questions.q: How do you use hostvars, groups and inventory_hostname to build cluster configuration?
questions.text: Use groups to list peers, hostvars to read each peer's variables and facts, and inventory_hostname for the current node, sorted for stable output. Ensure facts are gathered for those hosts and beware of --limit hiding them. {% for h in groups['db'] | sort %} server {{ hostvars[h].ansible_host }}:5432; {% endfor %} Interview tip: Say sort groups and gather facts for peers.

questions.q: How do combine, json_query, selectattr and map help transform data in Ansible?
questions.text: Use combine to merge dicts, selectattr and rejectattr to filter lists, map to extract attributes, json_query with JMESPath for nested JSON, and dict2items for mappings. Split long chains into named set_fact steps and write a custom filter if it gets heavy. - ansible.builtin.set_fact: names: "{{ users | selectattr('active') | map(attribute='name') | list }}" {{ r.json | json_query('items[?status==`ready`].id') }} Interview tip: Say small named steps beat long filter chains.

questions.q: How do add_host and group_by create groups dynamically during a run?
questions.text: add_host injects hosts and groups into the in-memory inventory for later plays, typically after provisioning; group_by creates groups from facts or expressions. Both last only for the run, so prefer dynamic inventory plugins for recurring needs. - ansible.builtin.add_host: name: "{{ item.public_ip }}" groups: new_web loop: "{{ created.instances }}" - ansible.builtin.group_by: key: "os_{{ ansible_os_family }}" Interview tip: Say add_host is run-scoped; inventory plugins persist.

questions.q: What naming conventions and structure do you use for variables to keep large automation manageable?
questions.text: Prefix role variables with the role name, name by meaning, keep defaults in defaults/, constants in vars/, environment data in group_vars, secrets in vault files referenced by plain variables, avoid deep nesting and document the schema. # group_vars/prod/vars.yml db_password: "{{ vault_db_password }}" # group_vars/prod/vault.yml (encrypted) vault_db_password: s3cret Interview tip: Say prefix, name by meaning, reference secrets indirectly.

questions.q: How do custom facts, facts.d and set_stats work?
questions.text: Drop .fact files or executables in facts.d to expose data under ansible_local, refresh with the setup module, cache facts if needed, and use set_stats to pass artifacts to later jobs in AWX workflows. - ansible.builtin.copy: dest: /etc/ansible/facts.d/app.fact content: '{"version": "{{ app_version }}"}' - ansible.builtin.set_stats: data: deployed_version: "{{ app_version }}" Interview tip: Say facts.d records host state; set_stats chains jobs.

questions.q: What is encrypt_string and when do you encrypt single values instead of whole files?
questions.text: encrypt_string encrypts a single value for inline use, keeping diffs readable but making rekeying and multi-line values harder. Whole-file vaults rotate easier; many teams use per-environment vault files and scan commits for plaintext. ansible-vault encrypt_string --vault-id prod@prompt 's3cret' --name 'db_password' Interview tip: Say per-environment vault files plus secret scanning.

questions.q: How do you use Ansible to scan and remediate compliance with OpenSCAP or CIS profiles?
questions.text: Run oscap with a CIS or STIG profile, fetch the reports, review generated remediation, turn accepted rules into a parameterised role, roll out in stages with check mode and a canary, track exceptions with owners and expiry, and rescan on a schedule. oscap xccdf eval --profile xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cis --results r.xml --report r.html /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-ubuntu2204-ds.xml ansible-playbook harden.yml --check --diff --limit canary Interview tip: Say review before applying; stage the rollout.

questions.q: How do you manage TLS certificates with Ansible, including generation and renewal?
questions.text: Use community.crypto to create keys and CSRs, acme_certificate for ACME, or sign internally; keep keys on the target with strict modes, reload services by handler, renew when remaining validity is below a threshold and back it with expiry monitoring. - community.crypto.openssl_privatekey: path: /etc/ssl/private/app.key size: 4096 mode: '0600' - community.crypto.x509_certificate_info: path: /etc/ssl/app.crt register: cert Interview tip: Say keys stay on the host; renew before expiry.

questions.q: How do you reduce SSH risk with bastion hosts, certificates and ProxyJump in Ansible?
questions.text: Route through a bastion with ProxyJump in ansible_ssh_common_args or ssh config, use short-lived SSH certificates instead of static keys, avoid agent forwarding, keep host key checking on, use dedicated limited accounts and log sessions. ansible_ssh_common_args: '-o ProxyJump=ops@bastion.example.com' [ssh_connection] ssh_args = -F ./ssh.cfg Interview tip: Say short-lived certs and ProxyJump, never disable host key checks.

questions.q: How do you audit what Ansible changed and who ran it?
questions.text: Run through AWX or CI for user and job records, log task results with callback plugins, keep Git history and approvals, use no_log for secrets, correlate with auditd and sudo logs on hosts, and stamp the commit or job id on the host. [defaults] stdout_callback = yaml callbacks_enabled = ansible.posix.profile_tasks, ansible.builtin.log_plays auditctl -w /etc/ssh/sshd_config -p wa -k ansible-change Interview tip: Say controller records, Git history, host audit logs.

questions.q: How do host patterns and the limit option select targets precisely?
questions.text: Combine groups with colon, intersect with &, exclude with !, match with wildcards or ~regex, pick by subscript, and narrow further with --limit or @file. Verify with --list-hosts and use a canary host first. ansible-playbook site.yml --limit 'web:&prod:!maintenance' --list-hosts ansible-playbook site.yml --limit @site.retry Interview tip: Say verify the target list before running.

questions.q: How do throttle, run_once and serial differ for controlling concurrency?
questions.text: Serial batches whole plays for rolling updates, forks caps overall parallelism, throttle caps concurrency for one task or block to protect shared services, and run_once executes a task on a single host, once per batch when serial is used. - name: Pull image community.docker.docker_image: name: app:1.2 source: pull throttle: 5 - ansible.builtin.command: /opt/app/migrate run_once: true Interview tip: Say throttle protects dependencies; serial protects availability.

questions.q: How do you profile Ansible runs with callbacks such as profile_tasks and timer?
questions.text: Enable profile_tasks, profile_roles and timer callbacks to find the slowest tasks, then fix the real causes: fact gathering, per-item loops, many small file copies, low forks and missing pipelining. Re-measure after every change. ANSIBLE_CALLBACKS_ENABLED=ansible.posix.profile_tasks,ansible.posix.timer ansible-playbook site.yml Interview tip: Say measure before tuning.

questions.q: How do you run Ansible against thousands of hosts across many networks and regions?
questions.text: Distribute execution with AWX instance groups or execution nodes per region, segment dynamic inventories, slice jobs, tune forks, pipelining and facts, roll out in canary waves with health gates, throttle shared services and consider pull mode for continuous convergence. ansible-playbook site.yml -f 100 --limit 'region_eu' -e 'serial_pct=10' Interview tip: Say distribute execution, slice inventory, roll out in waves.

questions.q: How do you handle hosts that are slow, flaky or temporarily offline during a large run?
questions.text: Set short connect timeouts, use ignore_unreachable, retries and async for slow tasks, collect failed hosts into a limit file for a re-run, use the free strategy and failure thresholds, rely on ansible-pull for returning machines and clean up the persistently dead. - hosts: all ignore_unreachable: true strategy: free ansible-playbook site.yml --limit @site.retry Interview tip: Say fail fast, retry later, clean up dead hosts.

questions.q: A playbook fails with SSH host key verification errors. How do you resolve them without disabling security?
questions.text: Do not disable host key checking in production. Distribute verified host keys via provisioning, ssh-keyscan from a trusted network or an SSH CA, remove stale entries with ssh-keygen after verifying new fingerprints, and relax checks only for disposable test hosts. ssh-keygen -R web01.example.com ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 web01.example.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts Interview tip: Say verify the new fingerprint out of band.

questions.q: A task hangs forever with no output. How do you diagnose it?
questions.text: Rerun with -vvv, inspect the process tree on the target, and look for prompts, package locks, non-detaching services, network calls without timeouts or sudo prompts. Add task timeouts, async, non-interactive flags and fix the cause. ansible-playbook site.yml -vvv --limit web01 ps -ef --forest | grep -A3 ansible environment: DEBIAN_FRONTEND: noninteractive Interview tip: Say look at the process on the host, not just the controller.

questions.q: A boolean or string comparison behaves unexpectedly, for example 'yes', 'true' and '0' in conditions. What is going on?
questions.text: Types get mixed between YAML, Jinja, command output and extra vars. Convert explicitly with bool, int and string filters, quote values, use JSON extra vars for typed input, inspect with type_debug and validate with assert. - ansible.builtin.debug: msg: "{{ port | type_debug }}" when: enable_feature | bool ansible-playbook site.yml -e '{"port": 8080}' Interview tip: Say convert explicitly; don't trust implicit truthiness.

questions.q: Variables named item or other loop variables collide or are undefined inside included tasks. How do you fix this?
questions.text: Nested loops and included task files overwrite the default item variable. Rename with loop_control loop_var, validate expected variables with assert, handle empty and skipped loops when reading registered results, and test with small data. loop: "{{ vhosts }}" loop_control: loop_var: vhost vars: vhost_name: "{{ vhost.name }}" Interview tip: Say give every loop its own variable name.

questions.q: A command or shell task is not idempotent and always shows changed. How do you make it behave?
questions.text: Prefer a real module. Otherwise use creates or removes, changed_when false for read-only commands, changed_when and failed_when based on registered output and return codes, or a prior check task, and enforce with Molecule idempotence. - ansible.builtin.command: /opt/app/setup.sh args: creates: /opt/app/.setup_done - ansible.builtin.command: grep -q enabled /etc/app.conf register: r changed_when: false failed_when: r.rc > 1 Interview tip: Say tell Ansible how to decide what changed.

questions.q: How do custom credential types work in AWX and the automation controller?
questions.text: A custom credential type defines input fields, secret flags and injectors that set environment variables, extra vars or temporary files at job time. Users can use the credential without seeing it, and plugins can fetch values from external secret managers. inputs: fields: - id: api_token label: API Token secret: true injectors: env: INTERNAL_API_TOKEN: "{{ api_token }}" Interview tip: Say users use credentials without seeing them.

questions.q: How do you manage AWX or the automation controller configuration as code?
questions.text: Use the ansible.controller or awx.awx collection modules, awxkit or the API to define organisations, projects, inventories, templates and workflows in Git, apply them from a pipeline, keep secrets as references, and reuse the definitions across controllers and for recovery. - awx.awx.job_template: name: Deploy app organization: Platform project: app-playbooks playbook: deploy.yml inventory: prod state: present Interview tip: Say treat the controller itself as code.

questions.q: How do job slicing and concurrency settings work in AWX?
questions.text: Job slicing splits the inventory into parallel jobs inside a workflow, reducing run time for independent hosts; it does not suit cluster-wide coordination. Concurrency uses allow-simultaneous-runs, instance group capacity measured in forks, and per-job forks. job_slice_count: 5 allow_simultaneous: false forks: 50 Interview tip: Say slice independent hosts only; match capacity.

questions.q: How do you troubleshoot AWX jobs that are stuck pending, fail to start or lose their output?
questions.text: Pending usually means no capacity, offline instances or a blocked project or inventory update; start failures are often execution environment image pulls or runtime issues; lost output points to receptor or resource pressure. Check instance capacity, dispatcher and receptor logs and pod events. kubectl -n awx get pods kubectl -n awx logs deploy/awx-task -c awx-task --tail=100 awx-manage list_instances Interview tip: Say check capacity first, then the job pod.

questions.q: What do Event-Driven Ansible rulebooks look like and what are practical use cases?
questions.text: A rulebook has sources that listen for events, rules with conditions on event data, and actions such as running a playbook or job template. Use it for self-healing and event responses, with precise conditions, rate limits, approvals for risky actions and full logging. - name: Disk alerts hosts: all sources: - ansible.eda.alertmanager: host: 0.0.0.0 port: 5000 rules: - name: Clean disk condition: event.alert.labels.alertname == "DiskFull" action: run_job_template: name: Cleanup disk organization: Platform Interview tip: Say start with safe, well-understood remediation.

questions.q: How do you automate VMware vSphere with Ansible?
questions.text: Use community.vmware modules and the vCenter inventory plugin with a least-privilege service account in vault, clone from templates, customise, wait for tools and IP, then configure the OS in a second play. Throttle vCenter and keep TLS validation on. - community.vmware.vmware_guest: hostname: "{{ vcenter }}" name: app01 template: rhel9-template state: poweredon wait_for_ip_address: true delegate_to: localhost Interview tip: Say provision in one play, configure in the next.

questions.q: How do you use dynamic inventory plugins for Azure and GCP?
questions.text: Use azure_rm and gcp_compute plugins configured in YAML with identity-based credentials, filters, compose for ansible_host and keyed_groups to turn tags or labels into groups. Enable caching for large estates and validate with ansible-inventory. plugin: azure.azcollection.azure_rm auth_source: auto keyed_groups: - prefix: env key: tags.environment ansible-inventory -i azure_rm.yml --graph Interview tip: Say tags become groups; verify with ansible-inventory.

questions.q: How do you automate database administration tasks with Ansible, such as users, schemas and backups?
questions.text: Use community.postgresql, mysql or mongodb modules to manage roles, grants and settings declaratively, keep credentials in vault with no_log, orchestrate backups with restore tests, leave schema migrations to migration tools, and gate risky changes. - community.postgresql.postgresql_user: name: appuser password: "{{ vault_appuser_password }}" db: appdb priv: ALL no_log: true Interview tip: Say declare users and grants; migrations belong to the app pipeline.

questions.q: How do you manage Docker or Podman containers and images with Ansible, and when is it appropriate?
questions.text: Use community.docker or containers.podman to pull pinned images and run containers declaratively with limits, restart policy and health checks, preferably as systemd units; appropriate for single hosts and edge cases, while larger fleets need an orchestrator. - community.docker.docker_container: name: web image: "nginx@sha256:{{ nginx_digest }}" restart_policy: unless-stopped published_ports: ['80:80'] state: started Interview tip: Say Ansible for small container fleets, Kubernetes beyond that.

questions.q: How do you roll out load balancer and reverse proxy configuration changes with Ansible without dropping traffic?
questions.text: Roll out one balancer at a time with serial, validate templates before activating, reload gracefully, health-check before continuing, drain backends before deployments and keep the previous config for rollback in a rescue block. - ansible.builtin.template: src: haproxy.cfg.j2 dest: /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg validate: 'haproxy -c -f %s' notify: reload haproxy - community.general.haproxy: state: disabled host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}" drain: true delegate_to: lb01 Interview tip: Say validate, reload, health-check, then next node.

questions.q: How do you verify the result of a role or playbook with Testinfra, Goss or assert tasks?
questions.text: Use assert with service_facts, package_facts and uri for in-play checks, and Testinfra or Goss as independent verifiers, ideally through Molecule. Test outcomes such as ports, services and permissions, run in CI and as production smoke tests. def test_nginx(host): assert host.package('nginx').is_installed assert host.service('nginx').is_running assert host.socket('tcp://0.0.0.0:80').is_listening molecule verify Interview tip: Say verify outcomes independently of the tasks.

questions.q: What does a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI pipeline for Ansible look like in practice?
questions.text: Merge requests run yamllint, ansible-lint, syntax-check and Molecule in a pinned tool image; main deploys to staging with smoke tests; production needs approval and serial rollout. Use short-lived credentials, pinned requirements, masked secrets and concurrency groups. ansible-galaxy install -r requirements.yml ansible-lint && ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check molecule test Interview tip: Say lint, test, stage, approve, roll out.

questions.q: What do you look for when reviewing Ansible pull requests?
questions.text: Review idempotency, module choice, conditions, handlers and variables; blast radius with limits, serial and guards; secrets and privilege; pinned dependencies and rollback; plus names, docs and passing lint and tests. Automation handles style so people focus on risk. ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff --limit staging git diff main -- roles/ group_vars/ Interview tip: Say review blast radius and secrets first.

questions.q: How do you upgrade ansible-core and collections safely when versions change and features are deprecated?
questions.text: Pin ansible-core and collections, read porting guides, run the test suite on a branch with the new version, fix deprecation warnings, check Python requirements for targets and promote through environments with rollback by reverting pins. Bots propose small frequent bumps. ansible --version && ansible-galaxy collection list ANSIBLE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS=true molecule test Interview tip: Say pin everything and upgrade in small steps.

questions.q: How do you document Ansible roles, playbooks and runbooks so other teams can use them?
